Migration is well-bounded: the entire UI is **165 lines in [llmtui/cli/](llmtui/cli/)**, and nothing in `agent.py`, `middleware/`, `tools/`, `sessions.py`, or `naming.py` knows a terminal exists. The restructure you just approved is what makes this a contained job rather than a rewrite — the blast radius is one directory.

Three pieces of work, ascending difficulty:

**1. Trivial — list rendering.** [cmd_list](llmtui/cli/commands.py#L18-L23) is pure formatting. Becomes a `DataTable`. The `[CURRENT]` prefix becomes a row style.

**2. Moderate — the blocking prompts.** [cmd_name](llmtui/cli/commands.py#L13), [cmd_load](llmtui/cli/commands.py#L32), and [cmd_delete](llmtui/cli/commands.py#L45) each stop mid-function on `input()`. Textual can't do that; they become `ModalScreen`s you `await self.push_screen_wait(...)`. Three functions, ~15 lines each. Two of them get *better* in the process: `/delete`'s whitespace-separated index parsing becomes a `SelectionList` (no more `isnumeric()` validation), and [the YES confirmation you commented out for testing](llmtui/cli/commands.py#L50-L52) becomes a real confirm dialog instead of a hardcoded `confirm = "YES"`.

**3. The real work — `stream_output`.** Two coupled problems in [render.py:16-46](llmtui/cli/render.py#L16-L46):

- It hardcodes `print(..., end="", flush=True)` as its sink.
- `agent.stream_events(...)` is synchronous. Iterating it inside a Textual handler freezes the event loop for the entire 27B response — which is exactly the multi-second window where you need the UI alive.

The second has a clean answer: I confirmed `astream_events` exists on `CompiledStateGraph`, so it's `async for` in a `@work` worker. No thread bridging, no `call_from_thread`.

The first wants one small refactor that's worth doing regardless of Textual: give `stream_output` a sink parameter instead of baking in `print`. The CLI passes `print`, the TUI passes `log.write`. Ten lines, and it makes the function testable for the first time.

**The `thinking_gate` wrinkle turns into a simplification.** The `<THINKING>`/`</THINKING>` inline tags exist because stdout has no other way to show structure — including [that awkward close-out](llmtui/cli/render.py#L40-L43) for tool-calling turns that end without a text delta. In Textual, reasoning goes to its own collapsible pane and answers go to a `Markdown` widget. The whole `thinking_gate` state machine disappears; you just route `reasoning-delta` to one widget and `text-delta` to another.

**What you'd gain that the REPL structurally cannot do:**

- `GraphRunStream.abort()` exists — a real "stop generating" binding. Right now ctrl-c kills the app.
- Tool results as collapsible panels. [print_tool_use](llmtui/cli/render.py#L50-L56) currently dumps five full passages inline with no truncation.
- Markdown rendering instead of raw text.
- That `"Watch for slight freeze, naming conversation..."` message becomes a status-bar spinner, since naming can run in a worker.

**Effort: an evening for something working, then polish.** Textual isn't installed yet (`pip install textual` + requirements).

My suggestion if you do it: build `llmtui/tui/` *alongside* `llmtui/cli/` rather than replacing it, with `app.py` picking via a flag. Both frontends consume the same `stream_output`, so the sink refactor is proven by the CLI still working. You keep a running app the whole time.

One honest caveat for the interview framing: the middleware is the most interesting code in this repo, and a TUI doesn't make it more visible. It does make the demo land harder, which is worth something. I'd do the sink refactor now either way — it's ten lines and it decouples rendering from streaming whether or not Textual ever happens.

llm-tui Textual Frontend

Replacing the print-based renderer with a Textual app that streams tokens live, settles them into rendered markdown, and shows retrieval happening as it happens instead of dumping passages afterwards.

01 What this has to do

Four requirements, and one of them quietly conflicts with another:

  • Keep the streaming. Tokens appear as the model produces them — reasoning and answer both. This is the thing that makes a local 27B feel alive instead of frozen.
  • Show the conversation properly. Turns as distinct blocks, scrollable, with the reasoning separable from the answer rather than fenced in <THINKING> tags.
  • Tool calls visible while running, concisely. One line per search, updating in place. Passages available on demand, never dumped into the flow.
  • Render markdown. Headings, lists, tables, code — the model already emits it, the terminal currently shows it raw.
The conflict: streaming wants to append one token at a time; markdown wants a complete document to parse. Section 02 is about resolving that, because getting it wrong is what makes TUI chat clients stutter.

02 Streaming into markdown

Textual's Markdown widget takes a whole string and builds a widget tree from it. update() re-parses the entire document. That's fine once; it is not fine sixty times a second against a document that keeps growing.

A · Stream raw, swap at the end

too coarse

Append plain text while streaming; when the message completes, replace the block with a rendered Markdown widget. Cheap and simple — what most LLM TUIs do. But the whole answer visibly reflows at the end, and for a long response you stare at unformatted text the entire time.

B · Re-render on a timer

the trap

Buffer deltas, call Markdown.update() every ~100ms. Looks right in a demo and degrades badly in practice: each tick re-parses everything written so far, so cost grows quadratically with answer length, and every tick reflows blocks that were already settled — the text jitters as it grows.

C · Settled blocks + live tail

chosen

Buffer incoming text. When a markdown block completes — a blank line outside a code fence — flush it into its own rendered widget and start a fresh buffer. The unfinished trailing block stays plain text in a single Static that updates as tokens land.

Already-rendered blocks are never touched again, so total work is linear. Formatting appears as soon as it is semantically complete. The only unformatted text on screen is the paragraph currently being written — which is exactly the part that should look like it is being typed.

Two details that make C work

  • Fence tracking. A blank line inside a ``` block is not a block boundary. The buffer needs a single boolean tracking fence state — otherwise code blocks get split in half and render as garbage.
  • Decouple token rate from frame rate. Don't touch the tail widget per token. Accumulate into a string and flush on set_interval(1/30). Ollama can emit faster than the terminal can usefully repaint, and this caps the work regardless.
Widget weight: for settled blocks use Static(rich.markdown.Markdown(text)) rather than Textual's Markdown widget. Textual's version mounts a subtree per block; Rich's renders to a single renderable inside one widget. Over a long conversation that is the difference between a few hundred widgets and a few thousand. The tradeoff is losing clickable links and the TOC — neither of which we want here.

03 Architecture

One App, one scrolling transcript, one input. The model runs in an async worker so the UI never blocks — this is the part input() made impossible.

TuiApp(App) ├─ Header model name, thread title ├─ VerticalScroll #transcript — turns mounted as they happen │ ├─ UserTurn │ ├─ AssistantTurn │ │ ├─ Collapsible reasoning, auto-collapses when answer starts │ │ ├─ ToolRow one per tool_call_id, mutates in place │ │ ├─ Static settled markdown block │ │ ├─ Static settled markdown block │ │ └─ Static #tail — live plain text │ └─ … ├─ Input prompt + / commands └─ Footer state, keybindings

The streaming worker

Input.Submitted fires a @work(exclusive=True) async worker that drives agent.astream_events(...) with async for. Because async workers run on Textual's own event loop, the worker can touch widgets directly — no call_from_thread, no queue. That is only required for thread=True workers, and we don't need one.

exclusive=True means a new submission cancels the previous run for free. A dedicated binding does the same deliberately, calling worker.cancel() and the stream's abort() — the current REPL has no way to stop a generation short of killing the process.

Mapping Textual onto what we have

TextualDoes what for usReplaces
@work(exclusive)runs astream_events without blocking the UIthe blocking for in stream_output
VerticalScrollscrollback that survives the sessionterminal history
Static + rich.Markdownsettled, formatted answer blocksprint(text, end="")
Collapsiblereasoning pane, folded once the answer starts<THINKING> tags + thinking_gate
ModalScreensession pickers for /load, /deleteinput() inside commands.py
set_intervalthrottles tail repaints to 30fpsflush=True per token
BINDINGSesc to stop, ^C to quit, ^L clearKeyboardInterrupt handler
TCSS fileall styling, hot-reloadable—

04 Tool rows

One line per tool call, keyed by tool_call_id, mutating through states in place. Concise by default; the passages live behind a Collapsible so nothing is lost but nothing floods either.

⠋search_books"initiative order"running
⠙search_books"initiative" · dnd_phb_5erunning
✓search_books"initiative order"5 passages · 1.4s
⚠search_booksmalformed arguments → recovered 2 callsrepaired
✕search_booksblocked · run limit reached3/3 used
The repair row is worth building deliberately. The middleware is the most interesting code in this repo and it is currently invisible — it prints [REPAIR] to a console nobody is reading. A row that shows a malformed call becoming two working ones makes the thing you built legible to anyone watching, which is the whole point of a demo.

Where the state comes from

Rows are created from tool_call blocks as they appear in the assistant message, and resolved when the matching ToolMessage lands. Keying on tool_call_id matters more here than in a normal client: the repair middleware rewrites the assistant message and mints new ids for recovered calls, so a row keyed on position would attach to the wrong call. A dropped call arrives as a ToolMessage with status="error" — which is exactly the ✕ state above, already carrying its own explanation.

05 Layout

┌─ llm-tui ────────────────────────────── qwen3.8:27b ─┐
│                                                        │
│  You                                                   │
│  how does initiative work in draw steel                │
│                                                        │
│  ▸ reasoning  2.1s                                     │
│  ✓ search_books  "initiative order"      5 passages   │
│                                                        │
│  Assistant                                             │
│  In Draw Steel, initiative is not rolled. Instead:      │
│                                                        │
│   • Each round opens with a team decision             │
│   • The side that acts first alternates                │
│                                                        │
│  ▌                                                     │
│                                                        │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ > ▏                                                    │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ streaming · esc stop · ^C quit · /help                  │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Reasoning collapses to a one-line summary with its duration the moment the first answer token arrives — visible while it matters, out of the way afterwards. Tool rows sit above the answer in the order they fired. The ▌ is the live tail.

06 Module layout

llmtui/ ├─ config.py unchanged ├─ agent.py unchanged ├─ sessions.py unchanged ├─ naming.py unchanged ├─ middleware/ unchanged ├─ tools/ unchanged ├─ tui.py App, widgets, streaming worker ├─ tui.tcss all styling └─ cli/ ├─ render.py deleted ├─ repl.py deleted └─ commands.py logic kept, input()/print() shells move to screens

Everything below the UI stays untouched — the restructure put every non-UI concern outside cli/, so this migration is bounded to one directory. commands.py is the one grey area: its calls into sessions.py stay as they are, while the list-printing and index-prompting shells become modal screens. /delete improves in the process — a multi-select list instead of parsing whitespace-separated indices, and the confirmation you commented out for testing comes back as a real dialog.

On the single file: tui.py will land somewhere around 400 lines. That is fine as one module. If widgets start needing their own tests, split at tui/app.py + tui/widgets.py + tui/stream.py — but not before.

07 Build order

Each phase leaves a running app. Nothing is half-migrated at the end of a step.

  1. Shell + plain streamingInput, transcript, async worker, auto-scroll. Text arrives unformatted. Proves the worker never blocks — the single riskiest assumption.
  2. Settled blocks + live tailBlock-boundary detection with fence tracking, the 30fps flush, Rich markdown in the settled blocks.
  3. Tool rowsCreation from tool_call blocks, resolution from ToolMessages, the collapsible passages.
  4. Reasoning paneRoute reasoning-delta to its own Collapsible; auto-fold on first answer token.
  5. Command screens/name, /load, /delete as modals. Session switching reloads the transcript from the checkpoint.
  6. Abort + repair rowsesc-to-stop, then the repair and blocked states — the parts that make the middleware visible.

08 Open before coding

Three things I have not verified, each of which could shift phase 3.

1 · What the v3 event stream actually emits for tools. stream_output reads stream.messages and filters content-block-delta. Whether v3 also surfaces distinct tool-start and tool-end events, or whether rows must be inferred from message content, decides how phase 3 is written. Worth an hour of introspection against a live run before building on it.
2 · Whether abort() is safe mid-tool. GraphRunStream.abort() exists. What it does to an in-flight Milvus query, and whether the checkpoint stays consistent afterwards, is unknown. If it isn't clean, esc should only cancel between steps.
3 · How repaired calls appear downstream. The middleware rewrites the assistant message in place, keeping the original id for the first recovered call and minting new ones for the rest. Whether the stream replays the rewritten message or only the original determines whether the TUI can show the repair as it happens or only after the fact.

content.text:
Design doc: **https://claude.ai/code/artifact/ea86ed7a-6522-4769-a27b-237245913be6**

The headline decisions, so you can push back without reading the whole thing:

**The streaming/markdown conflict is the real design problem.** Textual's `Markdown` widget re-parses the entire document on `update()`. The obvious approach — buffer tokens, re-render every 100ms — is quadratic in answer length and makes settled text jitter as it reflows. I rejected it.

What I chose instead: **settled blocks + live tail.** Buffer incoming text; when a markdown block completes (blank line, tracked so it doesn't fire inside a ``` fence), flush it into its own rendered widget and start fresh. The unfinished trailing paragraph stays plain text in one `Static` that updates as tokens land. Rendered blocks are never touched again — linear total work, formatting appears as soon as it's semantically complete, and the only unformatted text on screen is the sentence currently being typed, which is exactly where you *want* a typing effect.

**Use Rich's `Markdown` inside a `Static`, not Textual's `Markdown` widget.** Textual's mounts a widget subtree per block; Rich's renders one renderable in one widget. Over a long conversation that's hundreds of widgets versus thousands. You lose clickable links and the TOC — neither of which we want.

**Async workers mean no thread bridging.** `astream_events` exists, so `@work(exclusive=True)` runs on Textual's own event loop and can touch widgets directly. No `call_from_thread`, no queue. `exclusive=True` also gives you free cancellation when a new prompt is submitted.

**Tool rows keyed by `tool_call_id`, not position** — this matters more in your repo than in a normal client, because the repair middleware mints new ids for recovered calls. A row keyed on position would attach to the wrong call after a repair.

**One thing I'd argue for:** build the repair row deliberately. Your middleware is the most interesting code here and it's currently invisible — it prints `[REPAIR]` to a console nobody reads. A row showing a malformed call becoming two working ones makes it legible to whoever's watching the demo.

**Three things I haven't verified**, all of which could shift phase 3 — and I'd resolve #1 before writing tool-row code, since it decides how that code is shaped:

1. Whether v3's stream surfaces distinct tool-start/tool-end events, or whether rows must be inferred from message content
2. What `abort()` does to an in-flight Milvus query and the checkpoint
3. Whether the stream replays the middleware's rewritten assistant message, or only the original — this determines whether repair can be shown live or only after the fact

Want me to spend a pass introspecting the actual event stream to close those, or start on phase 1 (shell + plain streaming), which doesn't depend on any of them?

What about using another library like https://github.com/charmbracelet/glow? Do a thorough research for what TUI library we can use, let's not repeat the same Milvus mistake where we are stuck with something not a 100% good fit.

Fair concern — and glow is a good prompt for it, because it exposes the real question: Charm's stack is Go, and that's an architecture decision, not a library choice. Let me research properly rather than assert from memory.

# Textual's Streaming Markdown Handling

Based on the article, here's what I found:

**What Problem It Solves:**
The traditional approach of removing and re-adding entire Markdown widgets became prohibitively slow as documents grew. McGugan needed a solution for rendering LLM API responses that arrive as token fragments rather than complete documents.

**Key Optimizations Implemented:**

1. **Finalized Block Preservation** – Only the final markdown block can change when new content arrives. Earlier blocks remain untouched, avoiding unnecessary widget recreation.

2. **Widget Update Efficiency** – Rather than replacing widgets, the system updates them in-place when the block type remains consistent (paragraphs, code fences, tables).

3. **Incremental Parsing** – Instead of re-parsing the entire document, only the final block's content is re-parsed, keeping parsing time "always sub 1ms" regardless of document size.

4. **Buffering Strategy** – A buffer sits between the token producer (LLM) and consumer (widget), concatenating rapid token arrivals to prevent UI lag from queued updates.

**Important Note:**
The article mentions this work "will shortly land in the Textual repository" but provides no specific version number, API method names, or class details like "MarkdownStream." McGugan notes that Toad features will appear in Textual's core library before Toad's release.

input.content:
Design doc · frontend

llm-tui Textual Frontend

Replacing the print-based renderer with a Textual app that streams tokens live, renders them as markdown while they are still arriving, and shows retrieval happening as it happens instead of dumping passages afterwards.

replaces cli/render.py + cli/repl.py today 165 lines agent code touched: none textual 8.2.8 · rich 15.0.0

01 What this has to do

  • Keep the streaming. Tokens appear as the model produces them — reasoning and answer both. This is what makes a local 27B feel alive instead of frozen.
  • Show the conversation properly. Turns as distinct blocks, scrollable, with reasoning separable from the answer rather than fenced in <THINKING> tags.
  • Tool calls visible while running, concisely. One line per search, updating in place. Passages on demand, never dumped into the flow.
  • Render markdown. The model already emits it; the terminal currently shows it raw.
The tension: streaming wants to append one token at a time; markdown wants a complete document to parse. Everything below hangs off how that is resolved, so the library question gets settled against that requirement specifically — not against "does it do markdown".

02 Library selection

The Milvus lesson was not that the library was bad — it was that it advertised a generic capability (hybrid search) and the specific thing we needed turned out to be missing or broken underneath: BM25 matching only exact terms, and AUTOINDEX silently selecting a dense index for sparse vectors. The gap only showed up against real data, after commitment.

So the test here is not "does it render markdown" but the specific thing: can it render markdown that is still arriving, without re-parsing the document on every token?

CandidateLangStreaming markdownVerdict
TextualPython native — MarkdownStream, incremental parse chosen
Rich LivePython re-renders the whole renderable per update fallback; no widgets or input handling
prompt_toolkitPython none — no markdown at all best-in-class input, wrong shape here
urwidPython none mature but dated; you build markdown yourself
Glamour / GlowGo excellent, but out of process architecture change, not a library swap
Bubble TeaGo via Glamour same — would split the app across two languages

On glow specifically

Glow is an application; Glamour is the library under it, and both are Go with no Python bindings. That makes it a process-architecture decision rather than a dependency choice, and there are only three honest ways to take it:

  • Shell out to glow per block. Works for rendering finished text, but spawns a process per render, cannot stream, and you still need a TUI framework around it. Strictly worse than what Python already offers.
  • Go frontend, Python backend, JSON-RPC over stdio. A real pattern — this is essentially what ACP does, and what Toad uses to drive multiple agent CLIs. But it puts a process boundary directly on the streaming hot path and doubles the languages in a repo whose whole point is the LangChain middleware.
  • Rewrite in Go. langchaingo is well behind LangChain Python, and the repair middleware — the most interesting code here — has no equivalent to port onto. Non-starter.

Charm's stack is genuinely nicer to look at than most. It is not worth a language boundary through the middle of a streaming path.

The finding that settles it. Textual added streaming markdown specifically because its author built Toad, a terminal client for AI agents, and pushed the fix upstream. The framework's newest work is being driven by exactly our use case. That is the inverse of the Milvus situation, where sparse search was a bolted-on secondary feature that defaulted to a broken index.

Risks accepted, stated plainly

  • Async is more code than sync. A recurring complaint, and true. The REPL is 40 lines; the app will not be.
  • Accessibility. Modern TUIs — Textual, Bubble Tea, Ink alike — are hostile to screen readers, because the cursor jumps on every repaint. Category-wide, not fixable by choosing differently.
  • Sustainability rests heavily on one maintainer. Mitigated by a permissive licence, a mature 8.x line, and releases every 2–3 weeks. Worth knowing, not disqualifying.
  • Old criticism, largely stale. "No menus or dialogs" dates from 2023; ModalScreen, Collapsible and friends exist now.

03 Streaming markdown

Every part of a Textual Markdown document is its own widget — each paragraph, code fence and table. Naively that is a problem: replacing the widget on every token gets slower as the document grows, and past roughly 20 appends per second the widget cannot keep up with the producer at all.

MarkdownStream is the supported answer, and it does exactly what a hand-rolled solution would have to do — except it is already written and tested:

  • Only the last block is ever re-parsed. Earlier blocks are finalised and never touched again, so parse time stays sub-millisecond no matter how long the answer runs.
  • Widgets update in place when the block type has not changed, instead of being torn down and rebuilt.
  • A buffer sits between producer and consumer. Tokens arriving faster than the widget can repaint are concatenated and delivered as one update, so Ollama's token rate is decoupled from the frame rate.
@work
async def stream_answer(self) -> None:
    md = self.query_one(Markdown)
    stream = Markdown.get_stream(md)
    try:
        async for chunk in ...:          # our astream_events loop
            await stream.write(chunk)
    finally:
        await stream.stop()
Verified locally, not assumed. On the installed textual 8.2.8: Markdown.append and Markdown.get_stream both exist, and MarkdownStream exposes start, stop, write. No version bump needed.
Reversing an earlier call. An earlier draft of this doc proposed hand-rolling block detection and rendering settled blocks as Static(rich.markdown.Markdown(...)) to keep widget counts down. That is now wrong on both halves: the block logic is upstream, and MarkdownStream requires Textual's own Markdown widget. Use the widget. The only reason left to reach for Rich's renderer directly is a non-streaming block such as a static help panel.

04 Architecture

One App, one scrolling transcript, one input. The model runs in an async worker so the UI never blocks — the thing input() made impossible.

TuiApp(App) ├─ Header model name, thread title ├─ VerticalScroll #transcript — turns mounted as they happen │ ├─ UserTurn │ ├─ AssistantTurn │ │ ├─ Collapsible reasoning, auto-folds when the answer starts │ │ ├─ ToolRow one per tool_call_id, mutates in place │ │ └─ Markdown driven by MarkdownStream │ └─ … ├─ Input prompt + / commands └─ Footer state, keybindings

The streaming worker

Input.Submitted fires a @work(exclusive=True) async worker driving agent.astream_events(...). Because async workers run on Textual's own event loop, the worker touches widgets directly — no call_from_thread, no queue. That is only required for thread=True workers, and we do not need one.

exclusive=True cancels a previous run for free when a new prompt is submitted. A binding does it deliberately via worker.cancel() and the stream's abort() — the current REPL cannot stop a generation short of killing the process.

Textual mapped onto what we have

TextualDoes what for usReplaces
@work(exclusive)runs astream_events without blocking the UIthe blocking for in stream_output
MarkdownStreamincremental markdown while tokens arriveprint(text, end="")
VerticalScrollscrollback that survives the sessionterminal history
Collapsiblereasoning pane, folded once the answer starts<THINKING> tags + thinking_gate
ModalScreensession pickers for /load and /deleteinput() inside commands.py
BINDINGSesc to stop, ^C quit, ^L clearKeyboardInterrupt handler
TCSS fileall styling, hot-reloadable—

05 Tool rows

One line per tool call, keyed by tool_call_id, mutating through states in place. Concise by default; passages behind a Collapsible so nothing is lost and nothing floods.

⠋search_books"initiative order"running
⠙search_books"initiative" · dnd_phb_5erunning
✓search_books"initiative order"5 passages · 1.4s
⚠search_booksmalformed arguments → recovered 2 callsrepaired
✕search_booksblocked · run limit reached3/3 used
The repair row is worth building deliberately. The middleware is the most interesting code in this repo and it is currently invisible — it prints [REPAIR] to a console nobody reads. A row showing a malformed call becoming two working ones makes what you built legible to anyone watching.

Where the state comes from

Rows are created from tool_call blocks as they appear in the assistant message and resolved when the matching ToolMessage lands. Keying on tool_call_id matters more here than in a normal client: the repair middleware rewrites the assistant message and mints new ids for recovered calls, so a row keyed on position would attach to the wrong call. A dropped call arrives as a ToolMessage with status="error" — the ✕ state above, already carrying its own explanation.

06 Layout

┌─ llm-tui ────────────────────────────── qwen3.8:27b ─┐
│                                                        │
│  You                                                   │
│  how does initiative work in draw steel                │
│                                                        │
│  ▸ reasoning  2.1s                                     │
│  ✓ search_books  "initiative order"      5 passages   │
│                                                        │
│  Assistant                                             │
│  In Draw Steel, initiative is not rolled. Instead:      │
│                                                        │
│   • Each round opens with a team decision             │
│   • The side that acts first alternates                │
│                                                        │
│  ▌                                                     │
│                                                        │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ > ▏                                                    │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ streaming · esc stop · ^C quit · /help                  │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Reasoning collapses to a one-line summary with its duration the moment the first answer token arrives — visible while it matters, out of the way afterwards. Tool rows sit above the answer in the order they fired.

07 Module layout

llmtui/ ├─ config.py unchanged ├─ agent.py unchanged ├─ sessions.py unchanged ├─ naming.py unchanged ├─ middleware/ unchanged ├─ tools/ unchanged ├─ tui.py App, widgets, streaming worker ├─ tui.tcss all styling └─ cli/ ├─ render.py deleted ├─ repl.py deleted └─ commands.py logic kept, input()/print() shells move to screens

Everything below the UI stays untouched — the restructure put every non-UI concern outside cli/, so this is bounded to one directory. commands.py is the grey area: its calls into sessions.py stay, while the list-printing and index-prompting shells become modal screens. /delete improves on the way — a multi-select list instead of parsing whitespace-separated indices, and the confirmation you commented out for testing returns as a real dialog.

On the single file: tui.py will land near 400 lines, which is fine as one module. If widgets start needing their own tests, split at tui/app.py + tui/widgets.py + tui/stream.py — but not before.

08 Build order

Each phase leaves a running app. Nothing is half-migrated at the end of a step.

  1. Shell + plain streamingInput, transcript, async worker, auto-scroll. Text arrives unformatted. Proves the worker never blocks — the riskiest assumption.
  2. MarkdownStreamSwap the plain sink for get_stream / write / stop. Should be a small diff, which is the point of using it rather than building it.
  3. Tool rowsCreation from tool_call blocks, resolution from ToolMessages, collapsible passages.
  4. Reasoning paneRoute reasoning-delta to its own Collapsible; auto-fold on the first answer token.
  5. Command screens/name, /load, /delete as modals. Session switching reloads the transcript from the checkpoint.
  6. Abort + repair rowsesc-to-stop, then the repair and blocked states that make the middleware visible.

09 Open before coding

Three things not yet verified, each of which could shift phase 3.

1 · What the v3 event stream emits for tools. stream_output reads stream.messages and filters content-block-delta. Whether v3 also surfaces distinct tool-start and tool-end events, or whether rows must be inferred from message content, decides how phase 3 is written. Worth an hour of introspection against a live run first.
2 · Whether abort() is safe mid-tool. GraphRunStream.abort() exists. What it does to an in-flight Milvus query, and whether the checkpoint stays consistent afterwards, is unknown. If it is not clean, esc should only cancel between steps.
3 · How repaired calls appear downstream. The middleware rewrites the assistant message in place, keeping the original id for the first recovered call and minting new ones for the rest. Whether the stream replays the rewritten message or only the original determines whether repair can be shown live or only after the fact.

content.text:
Doc updated at the same URL — new section 02 is the library evaluation, and section 03 reverses a call I got wrong.

**The research turned up something that changes the design, and it's the good kind of surprise.**

Textual ships `MarkdownStream`, reached via `Markdown.get_stream()`. I verified it against your installed 8.2.8: `Markdown.append`, `Markdown.get_stream`, and `MarkdownStream.{start, stop, write}` all present. No upgrade needed.

It does exactly what I proposed hand-rolling, but properly: only the final block is re-parsed (sub-millisecond regardless of document length), finished blocks are never touched again, widgets update in place when the block type is unchanged, and a buffer between producer and consumer coalesces tokens arriving faster than the terminal can repaint. So my "settled blocks + live tail" design was right in shape and unnecessary in practice — and my advice to use `Static(rich.markdown.Markdown(...))` for settled blocks was outright wrong, since `MarkdownStream` requires Textual's own widget. Both corrected in the doc.

**Why it exists is the part that answers your actual question.** Will McGugan built [Toad](https://willmcgugan.github.io/toad-released/), a terminal client for AI agents, hit precisely this problem, and [pushed the fix upstream into Textual](https://willmcgugan.github.io/streaming-markdown/). The framework's newest work is being driven by our exact use case. That's the structural inverse of Milvus, where sparse search was a secondary feature that defaulted to a dense index for sparse vectors and matched exact terms only — a generic capability that didn't cover the specific need, discovered after commitment.

**On glow:** it's an application; [Glamour](https://github.com/charmbracelet/glamour) is the library beneath it, and both are Go with no Python bindings. That makes it a process-architecture decision, not a dependency choice. Three honest paths — shell out per block (no streaming, spawn per render, still need a TUI around it), Go frontend over stdio JSON-RPC (real, it's roughly what ACP does, but it puts a process boundary on the streaming hot path), or rewrite in Go (`langchaingo` is well behind, and your repair middleware has nothing to port onto). Charm's output looks better than most. Not worth a language boundary through the middle of a streaming path.

**Everything else in Python fails the specific test:** [prompt_toolkit](https://python-prompt-toolkit.readthedocs.io/) has the best input handling available and no markdown at all — full-screen is a secondary feature it [grew later](https://github.com/Textualize/textual/discussions/3254). urwid is mature and dated with no markdown. Rich's `Live` re-renders the whole renderable per update and gives you no widgets or input handling — it's the fallback if you wanted zero new dependencies, not a frontend.

**Risks I'd want you to have seen, since the point was avoiding a late surprise:** the async model is genuinely more code than the 40-line REPL, and it's a recurring complaint. Modern TUIs across the board — Textual, Bubble Tea, Ink — are [hostile to screen readers](https://xogium.me/the-text-mode-lie-why-modern-tuis-are-a-nightmare-for-accessibility) because the cursor jumps on every repaint; that's category-wide, not avoidable by choosing differently. And sustainability leans heavily on one maintainer, mitigated by a permissive licence, a mature 8.x line, and releases every 2–3 weeks. The old "no menus or dialogs" criticism is from 2023 and stale — `ModalScreen` and `Collapsible` exist now.

Verdict: Textual, and more confidently than before I looked.

Phase 2 just got much smaller — swapping the plain sink for `get_stream`/`write`/`stop` is a handful of lines instead of a block parser. Want me to start on phase 1, or close open question #1 first (introspecting what the v3 stream actually emits for tool start/end), since that's what shapes phase 3?

Sources: [Efficient streaming of Markdown in the terminal](https://willmcgugan.github.io/streaming-markdown/) · [Textual Markdown widget](https://textual.textualize.io/widgets/markdown/) · [Textual releases](https://github.com/Textualize/textual/releases) · [Toad](https://willmcgugan.github.io/toad-released/) · [Glamour](https://github.com/charmbracelet/glamour) · [Textual vs prompt_toolkit](https://github.com/Textualize/textual/discussions/3254) · [prompt_toolkit full-screen apps](https://python-prompt-toolkit.readthedocs.io/en/stable/pages/full_screen_apps.html)
Give me a mock TUI design so we can get you to pin down the behaviour I want. Only after, we will implement.

Right — better to argue about a picture than about prose. I built a playable mock rather than static frames, since half the behavior you'd want to pin down is *timing*: when reasoning folds, when tool rows resolve, what the answer looks like mid-stream.

"""Answers two questions the TUI design depends on:
   1. what an async v3 run gives us, and how tool starts/ends surface
   2. whether ChatOllama reports token counts and timings we can put in the status bar

import asyncio, sys, uuid, json
sys.path.insert(0, "/home/ucak/projects/llm-tui")

from langchain_core.language_models import BaseChatModel
from langchain_core.outputs import ChatResult, ChatGeneration
from langchain.messages import AIMessage, HumanMessage
from langchain.agents import create_agent
from langchain.tools import tool


class ScriptedModel(BaseChatModel):
    responses: list
    def _generate(self, messages, stop=None, run_manager=None, **kwargs):
        return ChatResult(generations=[ChatGeneration(message=self.responses.pop(0))])
    @property
    def _llm_type(self): return "scripted"
    def bind_tools(self, tools, **kwargs): return self


def ai_valid(calls):
    tcs, blocks = [], [{"type": "reasoning", "reasoning": "thinking", "index": 0}]
    for name, args in calls:
        cid = str(uuid.uuid4())
        tcs.append({"name": name, "args": args, "id": cid, "type": "tool_call"})
        blocks.append({"type": "tool_call", "id": cid, "name": name, "args": args})
    return AIMessage(content=blocks, tool_calls=tcs, id=str(uuid.uuid4()))


@tool
def search_books(query: str, book: str = "") -> str:
    """Search the book library."""
    return f"PASSAGE for {query!r}"


async def probe_events():
    print("=" * 68)
    print("PROBE 1  async v3 run — what arrives, in what order")
    print("=" * 68)

    agent = create_agent(
        model=ScriptedModel(responses=[
            ai_valid([("search_books", {"query": "initiative"}),
                      ("search_books", {"query": "holding a turn"})]),
            AIMessage(content=[{"type": "text", "text": "Done."}], id=str(uuid.uuid4())),

    print(f"  __aiter__={hasattr(stream,'__aiter__')}  __iter__={hasattr(stream,'__iter__')}")
    print(f"  public: {[a for a in dir(stream) if not a.startswith('_')]}\n")

    seen = []
    if hasattr(stream, "__aiter__"):
        async for ev in stream:
            seen.append(ev)
    print(f"top-level async iteration yielded {len(seen)} items")
    for ev in seen[:40]:
        if isinstance(ev, dict):
            print("   dict keys:", list(ev.keys())[:8], "| event=", ev.get("event"))
        else:
            print("   ", type(ev).__name__, str(ev)[:90])

    if hasattr(stream, "messages"):
        print("\n  .messages present ->", type(stream.messages).__name__)


async def probe_ollama():
    print("\n" + "=" * 68)
    print("PROBE 2  ChatOllama token counts + timings (status bar 7b/7c)")
    print("=" * 68)
    import os
    from dotenv import load_dotenv
    load_dotenv("/home/ucak/projects/llm-tui/.env")
    from langchain_ollama.chat_models import ChatOllama

    m = ChatOllama(model=os.getenv("MODEL"), reasoning=False, num_ctx=2048)
    msg = await m.ainvoke([HumanMessage("Reply with exactly: ok")])

    print("usage_metadata   ->", json.dumps(msg.usage_metadata, indent=2, default=str))
    rm = dict(msg.response_metadata or {})

    ec, ed = rm.get("eval_count"), rm.get("eval_duration")

    chunks = []
    async for c in m.astream([HumanMessage("Count to three.")]):

    for i, c in enumerate(chunks):
        if c.usage_metadata:
            print(f"  chunk {i}/{len(chunks)-1} carries usage_metadata: {c.usage_metadata}")

def ai_valid(calls):
    tcs, blocks = [], [{"type": "reasoning", "reasoning": "r", "index": 0}]
    for name, args in calls:

        tcs.append({"name": name, "args": args, "id": cid, "type": "tool_call"})
        blocks.append({"type": "tool_call", "id": cid, "name": name, "args": args})
    return AIMessage(content=blocks, tool_calls=tcs, id=str(uuid.uuid4()))

async def drain(name):

    stream = await build().astream_events({"messages": [HumanMessage("q")]}, version="v3")
    n = 0
    try:

Where the state comes from

Rows are created from tool_call blocks as they appear in the assistant message and resolved when the matching ToolMessage lands. Keying on tool_call_id matters more here than in a normal client: the repair middleware rewrites the assistant message and mints new ids for recovered calls, so a row keyed on position would attach to the wrong call. A dropped call arrives as a ToolMessage with status="error" — the ✕ state above, already carrying its own explanation.
input.new_string:
Where the state comes from

Better than expected. The run exposes a dedicated tool_calls channel that yields one ToolCallStream per call, so nothing has to be inferred from message content: 

async for tc in stream.tool_calls:
    row = turn.add_row(tc.tool_call_id, tc.tool_name, tc.input)   # args, immediately
    tasks.append(asyncio.create_task(watch(tc, row)))

async def watch(tc, row):
    async for delta in tc.output_deltas:      # drains while the tool runs
        pass
    row.resolve(tc.output, tc.error)          # both populated once drained

tool_call_id arrives as the channel key, which is what the repair middleware makes necessary — it rewrites the assistant message and mints new ids for recovered calls, so a row keyed on position would attach to the wrong call. A tool that raises surfaces on tc.error rather than as an exception, so the error row is a normal branch.

One trap. tc.completed is a plain bool, not an awaitable — reading it when the stream object first arrives always returns False. Completion is signalled by output_deltas running dry. Each tool needs its own task, or the rows serialise and the concurrency the ToolNode already gives us is thrown away on the display side.

09 Open before coding

Three things not yet verified, each of which could shift phase 3.

1 · What the v3 event stream emits for tools. stream_output reads stream.messages and filters content-block-delta. Whether v3 also surfaces distinct tool-start and tool-end events, or whether rows must be inferred from message content, decides how phase 3 is written. Worth an hour of introspection against a live run first.
2 · Whether abort() is safe mid-tool. GraphRunStream.abort() exists. What it does to an in-flight Milvus query, and whether the checkpoint stays consistent afterwards, is unknown. If it is not clean, esc should only cancel between steps.
3 · How repaired calls appear downstream. The middleware rewrites the assistant message in place, keeping the original id for the first recovered call and minting new ones for the rest. Whether the stream replays the rewritten message or only the original determines whether repair can be shown live or only after the fact.

The status bar needs real numbers, and they exist

Both additions are backed by data ChatOllama already returns, so neither is an estimate:

  • Context meter. usage_metadata.input_tokens on the final assistant message is exactly what the turn cost to send, measured by the model rather than guessed from character counts. Against CONTEXT_SIZE that is the meter, and it is honest.
  • Tokens per second. response_metadata carries eval_count and eval_duration in nanoseconds, so generation speed is eval_count / (eval_duration / 1e9) — output only, excluding prompt processing, which is the number worth showing. prompt_eval_duration and load_duration are there too if the first-token wait ever needs breaking out.
Watch this one. While streaming, usage_metadata did not land on the final chunk — it arrived on the second-to-last. Capture it from whichever chunk carries it rather than reading the last one, or the meter silently stays empty.
Still genuinely open: whether abort() is safe mid-tool. What it does to an in-flight Milvus query, and whether the checkpoint stays consistent afterwards, is untested. Until it is, esc cancels the Textual worker rather than calling abort() — which stops the display immediately and lets the graph finish its step cleanly.

"""Textual frontend: a streaming transcript, live tool rows, markdown answers.

Replaces the print-based renderer. Nothing below the UI changes -- the agent,
the middleware and the tools are untouched, and this module only consumes what
the run already emits.

The run is driven through astream_events(version="v3"), which hands back an
AsyncGraphRunStream. That splits into named channels, and the two we care about
are consumed in parallel: .messages carries reasoning and answer deltas,
.tool_calls carries one ToolCallStream per call so rows can appear the moment a
search is dispatched rather than after the fact.
"""

import asyncio
import time

from langchain.messages import AIMessage, HumanMessage

from textual import on, work
from textual.app import App, ComposeResult
from textual.containers import Vertical, VerticalScroll
from textual.widgets import Collapsible, Input, Markdown, Static

from llmtui import config
from llmtui.sessions import list_sessions


SPINNER: str = "⠋⠙⠹⠸⠼⠴⠦⠧⠇⠏"
# how many blocks wide the context meter is drawn
METER_WIDTH: int = 8
# the reader has to be this many rows off the bottom before following stops
PIN_SLACK: int = 2


def meter(used: int, total: int) -> str:
    """A little bar showing how full the context window is."""

    if not total:
        return ""
    filled = min(METER_WIDTH, round(METER_WIDTH * used / total))
    return "▓" * filled + "░" * (METER_WIDTH - filled)


def compact(n: int) -> str:
    return f"{n / 1000:.1f}k" if n >= 1000 else str(n)


class ToolRow(Collapsible):
    """One tool call: a status line that expands in place into its passages.

    Keyed by tool_call_id rather than position, because the repair middleware
    rewrites the assistant message and mints fresh ids for recovered calls -- a
    row keyed on order would end up attached to the wrong call.
    """

    def __init__(self, tool_call_id: str, tool_name: str, args: dict) -> None:
        self.tool_call_id = tool_call_id
        self.tool_name = tool_name
        self.args = args or {}
        self._started = time.monotonic()
        self._spin = 0
        self._timer = None
        self._body = Static("running…", classes="passages")
        super().__init__(
            self._body,
            title=self._title(),
            collapsed=True,
            collapsed_symbol="▸",
            expanded_symbol="▾",
            classes="toolrow -running",
        )

    def _label(self) -> str:
        """What was actually asked for, short enough to sit on one line."""

        query = self.args.get("query") if isinstance(self.args, dict) else None
        book = self.args.get("book") if isinstance(self.args, dict) else None
        text = f'"{query}"' if query else str(self.args)[:52]
        return f"{text} · {book}" if book else text

    def _title(self, mark: str | None = None, meta: str = "") -> str:
        mark = mark or SPINNER[self._spin]
        line = f"{mark} {self.tool_name}  {self._label()}"
        return f"{line}   {meta}" if meta else line

    def on_mount(self) -> None:
        self._timer = self.set_interval(0.08, self._tick)

    def _tick(self) -> None:
        self._spin = (self._spin + 1) % len(SPINNER)
        self.title = self._title()

    def resolve(self, output, error) -> None:
        """Settle the row once output_deltas has run dry."""

        if self._timer is not None:
            self._timer.stop()
            self._timer = None

        elapsed = time.monotonic() - self._started
        self.remove_class("-running")

        if error is not None:
            self.add_class("-error")
            self.title = self._title("✕", f"{type(error).__name__} · {elapsed:.1f}s")
            self._body.update(str(error))
            return

        text = str(output or "")
        # search_books joins its passages with this separator, so splitting on it
        # gets the count back without the tool having to report one
        passages = text.split("\n\n---\n\n") if text.strip() else []
        self.add_class("-ok")
        self.title = self._title("✓", f"{len(passages)} passages · {elapsed:.1f}s")
        self._body.update(text or "(nothing returned)")


class AssistantTurn(Vertical):
    """One reply: the reasoning, the searches it fired, and the answer."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        super().__init__(classes="turn")
        self.reasoning: Collapsible | None = None
        self.reasoning_body: Static | None = None
        self.answer: Markdown | None = None
        self._md = None
        self._reasoning: list[str] = []
        self._reason_started: float | None = None
        self._folded = False

    async def write_reasoning(self, text: str) -> None:
        if self.reasoning is None:
            self.reasoning_body = Static("", classes="reasoning-body")
            self.reasoning = Collapsible(
                self.reasoning_body,
                title="reasoning",
                collapsed=False,
                collapsed_symbol="▸",
                expanded_symbol="▾",
                classes="reasoning",
            )
            self._reason_started = time.monotonic()
            await self.mount(self.reasoning)
        self._reasoning.append(text)
        self.reasoning_body.update("".join(self._reasoning))

    def fold_reasoning(self) -> None:
        """Once the answer starts, reasoning collapses to a one-line summary."""

        if self.reasoning is None or self._folded:
            return
        self._folded = True
        words = len("".join(self._reasoning).split())
        elapsed = time.monotonic() - (self._reason_started or time.monotonic())
        self.reasoning.title = f"reasoning · {elapsed:.1f}s · {words} words"
        self.reasoning.collapsed = True

    async def add_tool(self, tool_call_id: str, tool_name: str, args: dict) -> ToolRow:
        row = ToolRow(tool_call_id, tool_name, args)
        await self.mount(row)
        return row

    async def write_answer(self, text: str) -> None:
        if self.answer is None:
            self.fold_reasoning()
            self.answer = Markdown(classes="answer")
            await self.mount(self.answer)
            # MarkdownStream re-parses only the final block, so this stays cheap
            # however long the answer runs
            self._md = Markdown.get_stream(self.answer)
        await self._md.write(text)

    async def note(self, text: str, classes: str = "note") -> None:
        await self.mount(Static(text, classes=classes))

    async def finish(self) -> None:
        if self._md is not None:
            await self._md.stop()
            self._md = None
        self.fold_reasoning()


class StatusBar(Static):
    """State, context pressure and generation speed."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        super().__init__(id="status")
        self.state = "ready"
        self.ctx_used = 0
        self.tps = 0.0
        self.elapsed = 0.0

    def render_line(self) -> None:
        parts = [f"[b]{self.state}[/b]"]
        if self.ctx_used:
            parts.append(
                f"ctx {meter(self.ctx_used, config.CONTEXT_SIZE)} "
                f"{compact(self.ctx_used)}/{compact(config.CONTEXT_SIZE)}"
            )
        if self.tps:
            parts.append(f"{self.tps:.0f} tok/s")
        if self.elapsed:
            parts.append(f"{self.elapsed:.1f}s")
        parts += ["esc stop", "^q quit", "/help"]
        self.update("  ·  ".join(parts))

    def set_state(self, state: str) -> None:
        self.state = state
        self.render_line()


class LlmTui(App):
    """The app itself: input at the bottom, transcript above it."""

    CSS_PATH = "tui.tcss"
    TITLE = "llm-tui"
    BINDINGS = [
        ("escape", "stop", "stop generating"),
        ("ctrl+q", "quit", "quit"),
        ("ctrl+l", "clear", "clear transcript"),
    ]

    def __init__(self, agent, model, sqlite_connection, agent_thread_config) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.agent = agent
        self.model = model
        self.sqlite_connection = sqlite_connection
        self.agent_thread_config = agent_thread_config
        self._pin = True
        self._turn_started = 0.0
        self._out_chars = 0

    # ---------- layout ----------

    def compose(self) -> ComposeResult:
        yield Static(f"llm-tui   [dim]{config.MODEL}[/dim]", id="chrome")
        yield VerticalScroll(id="transcript")
        yield Input(placeholder="ask about the library, or /help", id="prompt")
        yield StatusBar()

    def on_mount(self) -> None:
        self.transcript = self.query_one("#transcript", VerticalScroll)
        self.status = self.query_one(StatusBar)
        self.status.render_line()
        self.query_one("#prompt", Input).focus()
        # following the tail is a repaint concern, not a token concern, so it
        # runs on its own clock rather than once per delta
        self.set_interval(1 / 15, self._follow)

    # ---------- scrolling ----------

    def _follow(self) -> None:
        if self._pin:
            self.transcript.scroll_end(animate=False)

    def on_mouse_scroll_up(self, event) -> None:
        # reading back through the transcript releases the tail
        self._pin = False

    def on_mouse_scroll_down(self, event) -> None:
        if getattr(self.transcript, "is_vertical_scroll_end", False):
            self._pin = True

    # ---------- input ----------

    @on(Input.Submitted, "#prompt")
    async def submitted(self, event: Input.Submitted) -> None:
        text = event.value.strip()
        event.input.value = ""
        if not text:
            return
        if text.startswith("/"):
            await self.run_command(text)
            return

        self._pin = True
        await self.transcript.mount(Static(text, classes="turn user"))
        self.run_turn(text)

    # ---------- the turn ----------

    @work(exclusive=True)
    async def run_turn(self, text: str) -> None:
        turn = AssistantTurn()
        await self.transcript.mount(turn)

        self.status.set_state("thinking")
        self._turn_started = time.monotonic()
        self._out_chars = 0

        try:
            stream = await self.agent.astream_events(
                {"messages": [HumanMessage(text)]},
                config=self.agent_thread_config,
                version="v3",
            )
            await asyncio.gather(
                self._pump_messages(stream, turn),
                self._pump_tools(stream, turn),
            )
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            await turn.note("⏹ stopped · esc pressed", classes="note stopped")
            raise
        except Exception as exc:
            await turn.note(f"✕ {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}", classes="note failed")
        finally:
            await turn.finish()
            self._read_usage()
            self.status.set_state("ready")

    async def _pump_messages(self, stream, turn: AssistantTurn) -> None:
        """Reasoning and answer deltas, in the shape the sync renderer used."""

        async for message in stream.messages:
            async for event in message:
                delta = event.get("delta")
                if event.get("event") != "content-block-delta" or not isinstance(delta, dict):
                    continue
                kind = delta.get("type")
                if kind == "reasoning-delta" and config.DISPLAY_THINKING:
                    self.status.set_state("reasoning")
                    await turn.write_reasoning(delta.get("reasoning", ""))
                elif kind == "text-delta":
                    chunk = delta.get("text", "")
                    self._out_chars += len(chunk)
                    self.status.set_state("streaming")
                    await turn.write_answer(chunk)

    async def _pump_tools(self, stream, turn: AssistantTurn) -> None:
        """One row per call, each watched on its own task.

        tc.completed is a plain bool and is False when the stream object first
        arrives, so completion is signalled by output_deltas running dry. Each
        call gets its own task, otherwise the rows resolve one after another and
        the concurrency the ToolNode already has is lost on the way to the screen.
        """

        watching: list[asyncio.Task] = []
        async for tc in stream.tool_calls:
            self.status.set_state("searching")
            row = await turn.add_tool(tc.tool_call_id, tc.tool_name, tc.input)
            watching.append(asyncio.create_task(self._watch_tool(tc, row)))
        if watching:
            await asyncio.gather(*watching)

    async def _watch_tool(self, tc, row: ToolRow) -> None:
        try:
            async for _ in tc.output_deltas:
                pass
        finally:
            row.resolve(tc.output, tc.error)

    def _read_usage(self) -> None:
        """Token counts straight from the model, rather than guessed from text.

        input_tokens on the last assistant message is exactly what the turn cost
        to send, and eval_count/eval_duration give generation speed excluding
        prompt processing -- which is the number worth showing.
        """

        elapsed = time.monotonic() - self._turn_started
        self.status.elapsed = elapsed
        try:
            messages = self.agent.get_state(self.agent_thread_config).values["messages"]
        except Exception:
            self.status.render_line()
            return

        for message in reversed(messages):
            if not isinstance(message, AIMessage):
                continue
            usage = message.usage_metadata or {}
            if usage.get("input_tokens"):
                self.status.ctx_used = usage["input_tokens"] + usage.get("output_tokens", 0)
            meta = message.response_metadata or {}
            count, duration = meta.get("eval_count"), meta.get("eval_duration")
            if count and duration:
                self.status.tps = count / (duration / 1e9)
            elif elapsed > 0 and self._out_chars:
                # no timings came back, so fall back to a rough client-side rate
                self.status.tps = (self._out_chars / 4) / elapsed
            break

        self.status.render_line()

    # ---------- commands ----------

    async def run_command(self, text: str) -> None:
        command = text[1:].strip()
        if command == "help":
            await self.transcript.mount(Static(
                "/help    this list\n"
                "/list    every conversation so far\n"
                "/name    title this conversation      [dim](phase 5)[/dim]\n"
                "/load    resume a conversation        [dim](phase 5)[/dim]\n"
                "/delete  remove conversations         [dim](phase 5)[/dim]",
                classes="turn note"))
        elif command == "list":
            current = self.agent_thread_config["configurable"]["thread_id"]
            lines = []
            for i, (thread_id, title, updated_at) in enumerate(list_sessions(self.sqlite_connection), start=1):
                mark = "[b]›[/b]" if thread_id == current else " "
                lines.append(f"{mark} {i}. {title or '(untitled)'}  [dim]{updated_at}[/dim]")
            await self.transcript.mount(Static(
                "\n".join(lines) or "no sessions yet", classes="turn note"))
        else:
            await self.transcript.mount(Static(
                f"{command} unrecognized. Try /help.", classes="turn note failed"))
        self._pin = True

    # ---------- actions ----------

    def action_stop(self) -> None:
        """Cancel the worker rather than abort()ing the run.

        Whether abort() leaves an in-flight Milvus query and the checkpoint in a
        consistent state has not been tested, so this stops the display and lets
        the graph finish its step.
        """

        for worker in self.workers:
            if worker.is_running:
                worker.cancel()
        self.status.set_state("stopped")

    def action_clear(self) -> None:
        self.transcript.remove_children()
        self._pin = True

"""Drives the Textual app headlessly with a scripted model.

Textual's run_test() pilot gives a real running app -- CSS parsed, widgets
mounted, workers scheduled -- without a terminal, so this catches broken TCSS
and bad mounts that only a live run would otherwise show.
"""
import asyncio
import sqlite3
import sys
import uuid
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))

from langchain_core.language_models import BaseChatModel
from langchain_core.outputs import ChatResult, ChatGeneration
from langchain.messages import AIMessage, HumanMessage
from langchain.agents import create_agent
from langchain.tools import tool

from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import MemorySaver

from textual.widgets import Collapsible, Markdown, Static

from llmtui.tui import AssistantTurn, LlmTui, ToolRow, compact, meter


class ScriptedModel(BaseChatModel):
    responses: list

    def _generate(self, messages, stop=None, run_manager=None, **kwargs):
        return ChatResult(generations=[ChatGeneration(message=self.responses.pop(0))])

    @property
    def _llm_type(self) -> str:
        return "scripted"

    def bind_tools(self, tools, **kwargs):
        return self


def ai_calls(calls):
    tool_calls, blocks = [], [{"type": "reasoning", "reasoning": "considering", "index": 0}]
    for name, args in calls:
        cid = f"call_{len(tool_calls)}"
        tool_calls.append({"name": name, "args": args, "id": cid, "type": "tool_call"})
        blocks.append({"type": "tool_call", "id": cid, "name": name, "args": args})
    return AIMessage(content=blocks, tool_calls=tool_calls, id=str(uuid.uuid4()))


def ai_text(text):
    return AIMessage(content=[{"type": "text", "text": text}], id=str(uuid.uuid4()))


@tool
async def search_books(query: str, book: str = "") -> str:
    """Search the book library."""
    await asyncio.sleep(0.02)
    return f"[core.pdf p.1]\nPassage about {query}\n\n---\n\n[core.pdf p.2]\nMore about {query}"


def build_app(responses):
    connection = sqlite3.connect(":memory:", check_same_thread=False)
    connection.execute(
        "CREATE TABLE sessions (thread_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT,"
        " created_at TEXT, updated_at TEXT)"
    )
    agent = create_agent(
        model=ScriptedModel(responses=list(responses)),
        tools=[search_books],
        checkpointer=MemorySaver(),
    )
    config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": str(uuid.uuid4())}}
    return LlmTui(agent, None, connection, config)


async def ask(app, text, settle=1.4):
    async with app.run_test() as pilot:
        app.query_one("#prompt").value = text
        await pilot.press("enter")
        await asyncio.sleep(settle)
        await pilot.pause()
        yield_state = {
            "tool_rows": list(app.query(ToolRow)),
            "markdown": list(app.query(Markdown)),
            "collapsibles": list(app.query(Collapsible)),
            "statics": [s for s in app.query(Static)],
            "status": app.status,
        }
        return yield_state


results = {}


def check(label, conditions):
    ok = True
    print(f"\n{'=' * 66}\n{label}\n{'=' * 66}")
    for desc, passed in conditions:
        print(f"    {'PASS' if passed else 'FAIL'}  {desc}")
        ok = ok and passed
    results[label] = ok


# ---- helpers are pure, check them first ----
check("0  helpers", [
    ("meter fills proportionally", meter(16384, 32768) == "▓▓▓▓░░░░"),
    ("meter clamps at full", meter(99999, 32768) == "▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓"),
    ("meter empty at zero", meter(0, 32768) == "░░░░░░░░"),
    ("compact shortens thousands", compact(8100) == "8.1k"),
    ("compact leaves small numbers", compact(412) == "412"),
])


# ---- 1. a turn with two searches ----
async def case_search():
    app = build_app([
        ai_calls([("search_books", {"query": "initiative", "book": "draw_steel"}),
                  ("search_books", {"query": "holding a turn"})]),
        ai_text("In **Draw Steel**, initiative is not rolled.\n\n- Teams alternate\n"),
    ])
    async with app.run_test() as pilot:
        app.query_one("#prompt").value = "how does initiative work"
        await pilot.press("enter")
        await asyncio.sleep(1.6)
        await pilot.pause()

        rows = list(app.query(ToolRow))
        answers = list(app.query(Markdown))
        turns = list(app.query(AssistantTurn))

        check("1  two searches -> two rows, answer rendered", [
            ("a tool row per call", len(rows) == 2),
            ("rows keyed by tool_call_id",
             {r.tool_call_id for r in rows} == {"call_0", "call_1"}),
            ("both rows resolved ok", all(r.has_class("-ok") for r in rows)),
            ("no row left spinning", not any(r.has_class("-running") for r in rows)),
            ("titles report passage counts",
             all("2 passages" in str(r.title) for r in rows)),
            ("book argument shown in the label",
             any("draw_steel" in str(r.title) for r in rows)),
            ("answer mounted as a Markdown widget", len(answers) == 1),
            ("reasoning pane created", turns and turns[0].reasoning is not None),
            ("reasoning folded once the answer began",
             turns and turns[0].reasoning is not None and turns[0].reasoning.collapsed),
            ("fold summary names a duration",
             turns and "reasoning ·" in str(turns[0].reasoning.title)),
            ("status returned to ready", app.status.state == "ready"),
        ])


# ---- 2. plain answer, no tools ----
async def case_plain():
    app = build_app([ai_text("Just an answer, no search needed.")])
    async with app.run_test() as pilot:
        app.query_one("#prompt").value = "hello"
        await pilot.press("enter")
        await asyncio.sleep(1.0)
        await pilot.pause()
        check("2  no tools -> no rows, still answers", [
            ("no tool rows", len(list(app.query(ToolRow))) == 0),
            ("answer still rendered", len(list(app.query(Markdown))) == 1),
            ("status ready", app.status.state == "ready"),
        ])


# ---- 3. a failing tool ----
async def case_error():
    @tool
    async def search_books(query: str, book: str = "") -> str:
        """Search the book library."""
        raise RuntimeError("simulated milvus GOAWAY")

    connection = sqlite3.connect(":memory:", check_same_thread=False)
    connection.execute("CREATE TABLE sessions (thread_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT,"
                       " created_at TEXT, updated_at TEXT)")
    agent = create_agent(
        model=ScriptedModel(responses=[
            ai_calls([("search_books", {"query": "grappling"})]),
            ai_text("The library is unavailable."),
        ]),
        tools=[search_books],
        checkpointer=MemorySaver(),
    )
    app = LlmTui(agent, None, connection, {"configurable": {"thread_id": str(uuid.uuid4())}})

    async with app.run_test() as pilot:
        app.query_one("#prompt").value = "grappling rules"
        await pilot.press("enter")
        await asyncio.sleep(1.4)
        await pilot.pause()
        rows = list(app.query(ToolRow))
        check("3  tool raises -> error row, app survives", [
            ("a row was still created", len(rows) == 1),
            ("row marked as error", rows and rows[0].has_class("-error")),
            ("row is not stuck running", rows and not rows[0].has_class("-running")),
            ("app did not crash", app.status.state == "ready"),
        ])


# ---- 4. slash commands ----
async def case_commands():
    app = build_app([])
    async with app.run_test() as pilot:
        app.query_one("#prompt").value = "/help"
        await pilot.press("enter")
        await pilot.pause()
        help_shown = any("/list" in str(getattr(s, "renderable", ""))
                         for s in app.query(Static))

        app.query_one("#prompt").value = "/nonsense"
        await pilot.press("enter")
        await pilot.pause()
        rejected = any("unrecognized" in str(getattr(s, "renderable", ""))
                       for s in app.query(Static))

        app.query_one("#prompt").value = ""
        await pilot.press("enter")
        await pilot.pause()

        check("4  slash commands handled in the same input", [
            ("/help lists the commands", help_shown),
            ("unknown command rejected, not sent to the model", rejected),
            ("empty submit is a no-op", len(list(app.query(AssistantTurn))) == 0),
        ])


async def main():
    await case_search()
    await case_plain()
    await case_error()
    await case_commands()

    print("\n" + "=" * 66)
    print("SUMMARY")
    print("=" * 66)
    for label, ok in results.items():

Both suites green. Everything is staged and uncommitted for your review.

**Built:** [llmtui/tui.py](llmtui/tui.py) (~400 lines), [llmtui/tui.tcss](llmtui/tui.tcss), [tests/test_tui.py](tests/test_tui.py), and [app.py](app.py) rewired to launch it. Phases 1–4 plus your status bar: streaming transcript, `MarkdownStream` answers, live tool rows keyed by `tool_call_id`, reasoning pane that auto-folds with duration and word count, context meter from real `usage_metadata`, and tok/s from `eval_count / eval_duration`.

The tests drive the app headlessly through Textual's `run_test()` pilot — real CSS parsing, real mounts, real workers, no terminal. That caught four bugs that would each have been an interactive debugging session:

**`render_line` is core Textual API.** `Widget.render_line(y) -> Strip`. My same-named status bar method meant the app couldn't paint at all — instant traceback on first frame.

**`Collapsible.__init__` assigns `self._title` as an instance attribute** holding a `CollapsibleTitle` widget, which shadowed my `_title()` method. Every `resolve()` threw `'CollapsibleTitle' object is not callable`, so rows got their CSS class but never their text — and because the class landed first, three of four assertions still passed. That's the kind of half-failure that reads as working.

**`tc.output` is a `ToolMessage`, not the string the tool returned.** Splitting `str(output)` on the passage separator found nothing, so every row reported "1 passages" regardless.

**`tc.error` is a plain string, not an exception.** `type(error).__name__` was producing titles reading `str · 0.0s`. Now it shows the first line of the actual message.

One design correction worth knowing: with `ToolErrorMiddleware` wired in, `tc.error` gets set *and* `tc.output` is `None` — the handler's guidance never reaches the stream object, it goes to the model through the message channel. My first instinct was to surface that guidance in the row, which was wrong: `on_search_error`'s text is instruction written for the model ("do not answer from general knowledge"), not something a reader needs. The row shows the failure; the model gets its coaching separately. Case 5 exists specifically because my original test built a bare agent and missed this whole path.

**Not done:** phase 5 — `/name`, `/load`, `/delete` as modals. `/help` and `/list` work; the other three print a phase-5 note. I deliberately left [llmtui/cli/render.py](llmtui/cli/render.py) and [llmtui/cli/repl.py](llmtui/cli/repl.py) in place despite the design saying they go, because **no human has driven this against real Ollama yet.** Headless tests prove the wiring, not that it feels right at 24 tok/s with a 27B model. Keep the working REPL until you've run `python app.py` and are happy.

That's the next thing: run it. Streaming smoothness, whether the spinner cadence is right, and whether reasoning folding is too abrupt are all things only a live turn will tell you.

=== sessions.py ===
"""The sessions table: the human-readable names sitting beside LangGraph's threads.

LangGraph's checkpointer owns `checkpoints` and `writes` and knows nothing about
titles, so a session's name lives in a table of our own keyed by the same
thread_id. Deleting a session has to clear all three.
"""

import sqlite3

from llmtui.config import SQLITE_DB_PATH


def connect() -> sqlite3.Connection:
    """Open the checkpoint database and make sure our own table is there."""

    sqlite_connection = sqlite3.connect(SQLITE_DB_PATH, check_same_thread=False)
    sqlite_connection.execute("""
        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sessions (
            thread_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
            title TEXT,
            created_at TEXT DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
            updated_at TEXT DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
        )
    """)
    sqlite_connection.commit()

    return sqlite_connection


def is_session_named(sqlite_connection, thread_id: str) -> bool:
    row = sqlite_connection.execute(
        "SELECT 1 FROM sessions WHERE thread_id = ?", (thread_id,)
    ).fetchone()
    return row is not None


def delete_session(sqlite_connection, thread_id: str) -> None:
    sqlite_connection.execute("DELETE FROM checkpoints WHERE thread_id = ?", (thread_id,))
    sqlite_connection.execute("DELETE FROM writes WHERE thread_id = ?", (thread_id,))
    sqlite_connection.execute("DELETE FROM sessions WHERE thread_id = ?", (thread_id,))
    sqlite_connection.commit()


def set_session_title(sqlite_connection, thread_id:str, title:str) -> None:
    sqlite_connection.execute("""
        INSERT INTO sessions (thread_id, title, updated_at)
        VALUES (?, ?, datetime('now'))
        ON CONFLICT(thread_id) DO UPDATE SET title = excluded.title, updated_at = excluded.updated_at
        """,
        (thread_id, title)
    )
    sqlite_connection.commit()

    return


def list_sessions(sqlite_connection):
    return sqlite_connection.execute(
        "SELECT thread_id, title, updated_at FROM sessions ORDER BY updated_at DESC"
    ).fetchall()

# ---------- the turn ----------

    @work(exclusive=True)
    async def run_turn(self, text: str) -> None:
        turn = AssistantTurn()
        await self.transcript.mount(turn)

        self.status.set_state("thinking")
        self._turn_started = time.monotonic()
        self._out_chars = 0

        try:
            stream = await self.agent.astream_events(
                {"messages": [HumanMessage(text)]},
                config=self.agent_thread_config,
                version="v3",
            )
            await asyncio.gather(
                self._pump_messages(stream, turn),
                self._pump_tools(stream, turn),
            )
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            await turn.note("⏹ stopped · esc pressed", classes="note stopped")
            raise
        except Exception as exc:
            await turn.note(f"✕ {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}", classes="note failed")
        finally:
            await turn.finish()
            self._read_usage()
            self.status.set_state("ready")

    async def _pump_messages(self, stream, turn: AssistantTurn) -> None:
        """Reasoning and answer deltas, in the shape the sync renderer used."""

        async for message in stream.messages:
        """Token counts straight from the model, rather than guessed from text.

        input_tokens on the last assistant message is exactly what the turn cost
        to send, and eval_count/eval_duration give generation speed excluding
        prompt processing -- which is the number worth showing.
        """

        elapsed = time.monotonic() - self._turn_started
        self.status.elapsed = elapsed
        try:
            messages = self.agent.get_state(self.agent_thread_config).values["messages"]
        except Exception:
            self.status.refresh_line()
            return

        for message in reversed(messages):
            if not isinstance(message, AIMessage):
                continue
            usage = message.usage_metadata or {}
            if usage.get("input_tokens"):
                self.status.ctx_used = usage["input_tokens"] + usage.get("output_tokens", 0)
            meta = message.response_metadata or {}
            count, duration = meta.get("eval_count"), meta.get("eval_duration")
            if count and duration:
                self.status.tps = count / (duration / 1e9)
            elif elapsed > 0 and self._out_chars:
                # no timings came back, so fall back to a rough client-side rate
                self.status.tps = (self._out_chars / 4) / elapsed
            break

        self.status.refresh_line()

        command = text[1:].strip()
        if command == "help":

                "/load    resume a conversation        [dim](phase 5)[/dim]\n"

                classes="turn note"))
        elif command == "list":

            lines = []
            for i, (thread_id, title, updated_at) in enumerate(list_sessions(self.sqlite_connection), start=1):
                mark = "[b]›[/b]" if thread_id == current else " "
                lines.append(f"{mark} {i}. {title or '(untitled)'}  [dim]{updated_at}[/dim]")
            await self.transcript.mount(Static(
                "\n".join(lines) or "no sessions yet", classes="turn note"))
        else:
            await self.transcript.mount(Static(
                f"{command} unrecognized. Try /help.", classes="turn note failed"))
        self._pin = True

    # ---------- actions ----------

    def action_stop(self) -> None:
        """Cancel the worker rather than abort()ing the run.

        Whether abort() leaves an in-flight Milvus query and the checkpoint in a
        consistent state has not been tested, so this stops the display and lets
        the graph finish its step.
        """

        for worker in self.workers:
            if worker.is_running:
                worker.cancel()
        self.status.set_state("stopped")

    def action_clear(self) -> None:
        self.transcript.remove_children()
        self._pin = True
