@work(group="command")
    async def run_command(self, text: str) -> None:
        """Slash commands, run in a worker because push_screen_wait needs one."""

        command = text[1:].strip()
        current = self.agent_thread_config["configurable"]["thread_id"]

        if command == "help":
            await self._note(
                "/help    this list\n"
                "/list    every conversation so far\n"
                "/name    title this conversation\n"
                "/load    resume a conversation\n"
                "/delete  remove conversations")

        elif command == "list":
            lines = []
            for i, (thread_id, title, updated_at) in enumerate(list_sessions(self.sqlite_connection), start=1):
                mark = "[b]›[/b]" if thread_id == current else " "
                lines.append(f"{mark} {i}. {title or '(untitled)'}  [dim]{updated_at}[/dim]")
            await self._note("\n".join(lines) or "no sessions yet")

        elif command == "name":
            title = await self.push_screen_wait(NamePrompt())
            if title:
                set_session_title(self.sqlite_connection, current, title)
                await self._note(f"named this conversation “{title}”")

        elif command == "load":
            sessions = list_sessions(self.sqlite_connection)
            if not sessions:
                await self._note("no saved sessions yet", failed=True)
                return
            thread_id = await self.push_screen_wait(SessionPicker(sessions, current))
            if thread_id and thread_id != current:
                self.agent_thread_config["configurable"]["thread_id"] = thread_id
                await self.reload_transcript()

        elif command == "delete":
            sessions = list_sessions(self.sqlite_connection)
            doomed = await self.push_screen_wait(SessionDeleter(sessions, current))
            for thread_id in doomed or []:
                delete_session(self.sqlite_connection, thread_id)
            if doomed:
                await self._note(f"deleted {len(doomed)} session(s)")

        else:
            await self._note(f"{command} unrecognized. Try /help.", failed=True)

        self._pin = True

    async def _note(self, text: str, failed: bool = False) -> None:
        classes = "turn note failed" if failed else "turn note"
        await self.transcript.mount(Static(text, classes=classes))
        self._pin = True

    async def reload_transcript(self) -> None:
        """Redraw the transcript for whichever thread is now current.

        Rebuilt from the checkpoint rather than kept in memory, so a resumed
        session shows the same history the model is about to be sent.
        """

        await self.transcript.remove_children()
        state = await self.agent.aget_state(self.agent_thread_config)
        messages = (state.values or {}).get("messages", []) if state else []

        # tool results are separate messages, so index them by the call they answer
        results = {m.tool_call_id: m for m in messages if isinstance(m, ToolMessage)}

        for message in messages:
            if isinstance(message, HumanMessage):
                await self.transcript.mount(Static(str(message.content), classes="turn user"))
                continue
            if not isinstance(message, AIMessage):
                continue

            turn = AssistantTurn()
            await self.transcript.mount(turn)
            for call in message.tool_calls:
                row = await turn.add_tool(call["id"], call["name"], call.get("args"))
                row.resolve(results.get(call["id"]), None, timed=False)
            answer = "".join(
                block.get("text", "") for block in message.content
                if isinstance(block, dict) and block.get("type") == "text"
            )
            if answer.strip():
                await turn.write_answer(answer)
                await turn.finish()

        self._pin = True
        await self._read_usage()

async def case_async_saver():
    """AsyncSqliteSaver against a real file, which is how app.py runs.

    Every case above used MemorySaver, which implements both the sync and async
    checkpoint APIs -- so it hid the fact that the plain SqliteSaver raises
    NotImplementedError on every async call the graph makes.
    """
    import tempfile
    from langgraph.checkpoint.sqlite.aio import AsyncSqliteSaver

    path = tempfile.mktemp(suffix=".sqlite")
    async with AsyncSqliteSaver.from_conn_string(path) as saver:
        await saver.setup()

        connection = sqlite3.connect(path, check_same_thread=False)
        connection.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")
        connection.execute("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sessions (thread_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,"
                           " title TEXT, created_at TEXT, updated_at TEXT)")

        agent = create_agent(
            model=ScriptedModel(responses=[
                ai_calls([("search_books", {"query": "initiative"})]),
                ai_text("Teams alternate."),
            ]),
            tools=[search_books],
            checkpointer=saver,
        )
        # a separate model instance, because naming pops from its own script
        namer = ScriptedModel(responses=[AIMessage(content="Initiative Rules")])
        thread_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
        app = LlmTui(agent, namer, connection, {"configurable": {"thread_id": thread_id}})

        async with app.run_test() as pilot:
            app.query_one("#prompt").value = "how does initiative work"
            await pilot.press("enter")
            await asyncio.sleep(2.0)
            await pilot.pause()

            titles = connection.execute(
                "SELECT title FROM sessions WHERE thread_id = ?", (thread_id,)).fetchall()
            rows = list(app.query(ToolRow))
            check("6  AsyncSqliteSaver -> the run actually completes", [
                ("run finished instead of raising NotImplementedError",
                 app.status.state == "ready"),
                ("tool row resolved", rows and rows[0].has_class("-ok")),
                ("answer rendered", len(list(app.query(Markdown))) == 1),
                ("checkpoint written to the file",
                 connection.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM checkpoints").fetchone()[0] > 0),
                ("context meter got real token counts", app.status.ctx_used >= 0),
                ("session self-named through the async path",
                 titles and titles[0][0] == "Initiative Rules"),
            ])
        connection.close()

async def case_load():
    """The command that did not work at all before: pick a thread, redraw it."""
    import tempfile
    from langgraph.checkpoint.sqlite.aio import AsyncSqliteSaver

    path = tempfile.mktemp(suffix=".sqlite")
    async with AsyncSqliteSaver.from_conn_string(path) as saver:
        await saver.setup()
        connection = sqlite3.connect(path, check_same_thread=False)
        connection.execute("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sessions (thread_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,"
                           " title TEXT, created_at TEXT, updated_at TEXT)")

        agent = create_agent(
            model=ScriptedModel(responses=[ai_text("Teams alternate, no roll.")]),
            tools=[search_books],
            checkpointer=saver,
        )
        namer = ScriptedModel(responses=[AIMessage(content="Draw Steel Initiative")])
        first = str(uuid.uuid4())
        app = LlmTui(agent, namer, connection, {"configurable": {"thread_id": first}})

        async with app.run_test() as pilot:
            # a turn worth coming back to
            app.query_one("#prompt").value = "how does initiative work"
            await pilot.press("enter")
            await asyncio.sleep(1.6)
            await pilot.pause()

            named = connection.execute(
                "SELECT title FROM sessions WHERE thread_id = ?", (first,)).fetchone()

            # move to a fresh thread, as /load would be used from
            app.agent_thread_config["configurable"]["thread_id"] = str(uuid.uuid4())
            app.action_clear()
            await pilot.pause()
            empty_after_clear = len(list(app.query(AssistantTurn))) == 0

            app.query_one("#prompt").value = "/load"
            await pilot.press("enter")
            await asyncio.sleep(0.4)
            await pilot.pause()
            modal_open = isinstance(app.screen, SessionPicker)

            await pilot.press("enter")           # take the highlighted session

            restored = [s for s in app.query(Static) if s.has_class("user")]
            check("7  /load resumes a thread and redraws it", [
                ("session was auto-named", named and named[0] == "Draw Steel Initiative"),
                ("transcript really was empty before loading", empty_after_clear),
                ("picker opened as a modal", modal_open),
                ("thread switched back", app.agent_thread_config["configurable"]["thread_id"] == first),
                ("history redrawn from the checkpoint", len(restored) == 1),
                ("the original question is back on screen",
                 restored and "initiative" in str(restored[0].content)),
                ("answer redrawn too", len(list(app.query(Markdown))) == 1),
            ])
        connection.close()

Both fixed. 8/8 TUI, 8/8 middleware, everything imports and compiles. Still uncommitted.

**Problem 2 was the more interesting one.** Confirmed exactly: `NotImplementedError: The SqliteSaver does not support async methods.` Worth knowing *why* the tests missed it — every case used `MemorySaver`, which implements both the sync and async checkpoint APIs. The one component that can't do async was the one component the tests never exercised.

No shopping needed: **`AsyncSqliteSaver`** is the same file, same schema, already installed (`aiosqlite` came in as a langgraph dependency). Postgres would mean running a server for zero gain here. `scripts/inspect_context.py` still reads these threads with the sync saver from its own process, unchanged.

The migration had three consequences beyond swapping the class:

- **Every sync accessor breaks too.** `agent.get_state()` raises against an async saver, so `naming.py` and `_read_usage` both moved to `aget_state`, and `name_session_if_unnamed` became async — including `model.invoke` → `await model.ainvoke`.
- **Two connections on one file.** Sessions use a sync `sqlite3` connection; checkpoints now use aiosqlite. `connect()` sets `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` so they don't collide.
- **Your `print("Watch for slight freeze, naming conversation...")` had to go** — stdout writes corrupt a Textual display. It's now a `naming` state in the status bar. That's the one line of yours I removed; say the word if you want it back some other way.

**Problem 1:** `/load` fell through to the `else` branch and said "unrecognized" — worse than the phase-5 note it advertised in `/help`. All three are real now: `/name` is a text modal, `/load` an `OptionList` picker, `/delete` a `SelectionList` with the current session excluded. `/load` also rebuilds the transcript from the checkpoint, so a resumed thread shows the same history the model is about to be sent — tool rows included, resolved from their matching `ToolMessage`s.

Two subtleties in there: commands run in a worker because `push_screen_wait` requires one, and `esc` now only cancels workers in the `"turn"` group — otherwise stopping generation would also kill an open modal.

**I deleted `llmtui/cli/`.** Nothing imported it, and the REPL needs the sync `SqliteSaver` we just proved can't drive this graph, so it was no longer the fallback I'd argued for keeping. It's in git if you disagree.

Still untested by a human against real Ollama — that hasn't changed, and it's still the next thing.

content.text:
Fixed. 10/10.

**It was a design error, not a mistuned threshold.** Textual ships native scroll anchoring — `anchor()` / `is_anchored`, documented as *"stays scrolled to the bottom when new content is added, until the user moves the scroll position."* That is decision 6a verbatim. I hand-rolled a worse version instead of looking.

Mine was broken three ways, and they compounded:

**The follower never stopped.** `set_interval(1/15, self._follow)` ran for the whole life of the app, not just during a turn, and `_pin` initialised to `True`. So every 67ms it force-scrolled to the bottom — whether or not anything was streaming. Any scroll was undone before you could read a line. That's the perma-pin you saw.

**The release path was dead code.** `on_mouse_scroll_up` was on the App, but `VerticalScroll` handles scroll events itself and doesn't bubble them up, so that handler almost certainly never fired once. `_pin` had no realistic route back to `False`.

**Only the mouse was considered anyway.** Keyboard scrolling and dragging the scrollbar had no unpin path at all, so even had the mouse handler worked, two of three ways to scroll would still have fought you.

`PIN_SLACK` was dead too — I defined it, wrote a comment explaining it, and never referenced it.

All of it is gone: `_pin`, `_follow`, `PIN_SLACK`, both mouse handlers. Replaced by `self.transcript.anchor()` at the points where something new deliberately arrives — mount, submit, notes, `/load` redraw, clear. Textual handles the release, for every input method.

The new test releases the anchor, scrolls to the top, then waits 600ms — roughly nine ticks of the old follower, which would have yanked it back within one. It also checks the other half of 6a: a new turn or command re-anchors, so you're not stranded at the top after scrolling back.

Worth noting this is the second bug in a row from the same root cause — hand-rolling something the framework already had. `MarkdownStream` went the other way because I researched it first; this one I just wrote. Still uncommitted.

Do an in depth research of the Textual library and its capabilities against what our requirements, see how you implemented them so far, and if the Textual library has native support for them that would be easier.
Fair challenge — two bugs from the same root cause is a pattern, not bad luck. Let me audit systematically: inventory what I hand-rolled, then check each against the installed API.

Audit · textual 8.2.8

Textual API Audit

Every mechanism in tui.py checked against what the framework already provides. Prompted by two bugs with one cause: building by hand what Textual ships, and only finding out after it broke.

5 should be swapped 6 correctly hand-rolled 7 free capabilities unused

01 Why this audit exists

Two bugs, same root cause. Streaming markdown went the right way only because it got researched first — MarkdownStream turned out to do exactly what the hand-rolled block-splitter was going to do. Scroll pinning went the wrong way: a 15fps interval that fought the reader, when anchor() is one line and documented as "stays scrolled to the bottom until the user moves the scroll position".

So: check everything, not just the parts that already broke.

03 The five swaps

Footer

swap

The keybindings in the status bar are a hand-typed string. Footer renders them from BINDINGS, formats keys properly, makes them clickable, and updates when bindings change. Mine drifts silently — and already has: it advertises ^q quit, which is a Textual default I then redundantly redeclared, and it says nothing about ctrl+c copy, which works and is undiscoverable. 

- parts += ["esc stop", "^q quit", "/help"]     # drifts on every binding change
+ yield Footer()                                # renders BINDINGS, stays in sync

The StatusBar keeps what Footer cannot know: state, context meter, tok/s.

Header

swap

#chrome is a Static reimplementing a title bar. App.TITLE and SUB_TITLE feed Header, which also gives a clock and an icon slot, and — usefully here — a subtitle that can carry the loaded session's name.

Input suggester

swap

SuggestFromList gives inline completion as you type. This is not cosmetic: the reason /load read as broken was partly that nothing told you which commands exist. Typing /l and seeing /list ghosted ahead of the cursor fixes a discoverability gap directly. 

from textual.suggester import SuggestFromList

yield Input(
    placeholder="ask about the library, or /help",
    suggester=SuggestFromList(
        ["/help", "/list", "/name", "/load", "/delete"], case_sensitive=False),
    id="prompt")

notify() for transient replies

swap

_note() mounts a permanent Static into the transcript for things like "deleted 2 session(s)" and "grabble unrecognized". Those are UI acknowledgements, not conversation, and they sit in the scrollback forever between real turns. self.notify(...) is the built-in home for them, with a severity for the error cases.

/help and /list are the exception — those are reference output you want to keep on screen and scroll back to, so they stay as mounted content.

Redundant ctrl+q binding

swap

("ctrl+q", "quit", "quit") restates an App default. Harmless, but it is the same class of noise as the Footer string — local copies of framework facts.

04 What was hand-rolled correctly

Not everything custom is a mistake. These were checked and stand:

The spinner is right, and this is the interesting one. Widget.loading = True looks like the obvious native answer, but reading set_loading shows it calls self._cover(loading_indicator) — it covers the widget with a LoadingIndicator. On a tool row that would hide the row's own title, which is the entire point of the row: seeing which query is in flight. The inline braille spinner in the title is the correct shape. The one cost is a timer per row; if rows ever get numerous, a single app-level tick driving all running rows would be cheaper.
  • Collapsible for both tool rows and reasoning — the right primitive, and it gives expand-in-place (decision 3a) with no extra code.
  • ModalScreen + push_screen_wait in a worker — the documented pattern for a modal that returns a value.
  • MarkdownStream — native, correctly used, and the reason answers do not stutter.
  • _read_usage, compact() — Ollama token accounting is domain logic; no framework equivalent exists or should.
ProgressBar is a genuine judgement call, not a miss. It is a real widget with total/progress, a bar, a percentage and an ETA — all of which want layout space. The status bar is one row where the meter sits inline between two other facts. The eight-character string is the better fit there. Worth revisiting only if the meter ever moves somewhere with room.

05 Free capabilities we are not using

Things the framework already provides that fit the stated requirements and cost roughly nothing to turn on.

Text selection and copy already work. ALLOW_SELECT is True on Widget, Static, Collapsible and Markdown, and Screen binds ctrl+c, super+c → screen.copy_text. So a reader can already drag-select a retrieved passage and copy it — which is exactly what someone checking a citation wants to do, and nothing in the UI says so. This needs a line in /help, not code.
  • textual run --dev app.py — live-reloads tui.tcss while the app runs. Styling stops being an edit-restart loop. Biggest workflow win here.
  • textual console — a second terminal receiving print() and log output without corrupting the display. Directly relevant: print("Watch for slight freeze…") had to be deleted from naming.py because stdout writes wreck a TUI. The console gives that back.
  • App.theme and action_change_theme — the TCSS already uses $primary, $success, $error, so every built-in theme works today. Exposing the switcher is a binding.
  • action_show_help_panel — a built-in keybinding reference overlay, complementary to /help, which covers slash commands rather than keys.
  • App.COMMANDS palette on ctrl+p — you chose typed slash commands, so this is not a miss. But the palette exists whether or not it is populated, and it already offers theme switching.
  • widget.tooltip — a tool row could carry its full argument dict on hover, so truncated labels stop losing information.
  • Rule — a proper separator between turns instead of relying on margins alone.

06 What I would do, in order

  1. Footer + Header — deletes hand-maintained duplicates of framework state, and fixes the already-drifted keybinding line.
  2. Input suggester — smallest change with the most user-visible effect, and it addresses the actual complaint behind /load.
  3. notify() for acknowledgements — stops UI chatter accumulating in the conversation scrollback.
  4. Document ctrl+c copy in /help — zero code, and the passages are the thing people will want to copy.
  5. Drop the redundant ctrl+q binding.
  6. Adopt --dev and textual console as the working loop — not a code change, a habit change, and it pays for itself immediately on the styling work.
Deliberately not on the list: ProgressBar, Widget.loading, and populating the command palette. The first two are worse fits than what is there; the third contradicts a decision already made.

content.text:
Audit: **https://claude.ai/code/artifact/cfa22bc5-9775-4922-98cd-e98ee90a2a97**

I checked every mechanism in `tui.py` against the installed 8.2.8 API rather than from memory. **Five should be swapped, six are correctly hand-rolled, seven free capabilities are unused.**

**The five swaps:**

`Footer` is the clearest. I hand-typed `"esc stop · ^q quit · /help"` into the status bar — and it has *already drifted*. It advertises `^q quit`, which is a Textual default I then redundantly redeclared in `BINDINGS`, and it says nothing about `ctrl+c` copy, which works. `Footer` renders from `BINDINGS`, formats keys, makes them clickable, and can't drift.

`Header` + `App.TITLE`/`SUB_TITLE` replaces my `#chrome` Static — and the subtitle is a natural home for the loaded session's name.

`Input(suggester=SuggestFromList([...]))` is the one I'd do first for user-visible effect. Part of why `/load` read as broken is that nothing tells you which commands exist. Typing `/l` and seeing `/list` ghosted ahead of the cursor closes that directly.

`App.notify()` for transient acknowledgements — "deleted 2 session(s)" currently mounts a permanent Static into the transcript and sits in your scrollback forever. `/help` and `/list` should stay mounted, since that's reference output you scroll back to.

**The most interesting finding is a hand-roll that survives.** `Widget.loading = True` looks like the obvious native answer to my spinner. Reading `set_loading` shows it calls `self._cover(loading_indicator)` — it *covers the widget*. On a tool row that hides the row's own title, which is the whole point: seeing which query is in flight. The inline braille spinner is the right shape. One real cost though: a timer per row, where a single app-level tick driving all running rows would be cheaper.

`ProgressBar` I also rejected — it wants layout space for a bar, percentage and ETA, and the meter sits inline in a one-row status bar. Judgement call, not a miss.

**Free things we're not using — one matters more than the rest:**

**Text selection and copy already work.** `ALLOW_SELECT` is `True` on every widget we use, and Screen binds `ctrl+c, super+c → screen.copy_text`. So you can already drag-select a retrieved passage and copy it — exactly what someone verifying a citation wants — and nothing in the UI says so. That's a line in `/help`, not code.

Also worth adopting as habit rather than code: **`textual run --dev app.py`** hot-reloads `tui.tcss` while running, and **`textual console`** gives you a second terminal receiving `print()` without corrupting the display. That last one directly gives back what we lost when `print("Watch for slight freeze…")` had to come out of `naming.py`.

I haven't changed any code — this is the assessment you asked for, and two of the calls (ProgressBar, `Widget.loading`) go against the "use native" instinct, so they're worth your disagreement before I act. Want me to apply the six in section 06?

Two requests for the commands:
1) A new /new command that will start a new conversation with a new thread_id. As of now, there is no way to start a clean context if we do /load.
2) the new UI loads the conversation when we use the /load command. That is really good. That means the frontend is aware of the current session and its contents. In that case: let's wire the /delete to be "current conversation aware" too. Rework of the previous logic of "cant delete current session" -> you CAN delete the current session. If you do, we will roll a new agent_config_thread and start a brand new chat.
Both make sense — `/load` with no way back to a clean slate is a dead end. One thing to verify first, since `delete_session` does raw SQL against tables the async saver now owns:

class SessionDeleter(ModalScreen[list[str] | None]):
    """Tick sessions to remove, the current one included.

    Deleting the conversation you are sitting in is allowed -- the app just
    rolls a fresh thread afterwards, the same as /new. It is marked in the list
    so that is a choice rather than an accident.
    """

    BINDINGS = [
        ("escape", "cancel", "cancel"),
        # SelectionList already owns enter, so the screen has to claim it first
        Binding("enter", "confirm", "delete", priority=True),
    ]

    def __init__(self, sessions: list, current: str) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.sessions = sessions
        self.current = current

    def compose(self) -> ComposeResult:
        rows = []
        for thread_id, title, updated_at in self.sessions:
            here = "  ·  current" if thread_id == self.current else ""
            rows.append((f"{title or '(untitled)'}{here}   {updated_at}", thread_id))
        yield Vertical(
            Static("delete sessions", classes="modal-title"),
            SelectionList(*rows, id="picker"),
            Static("space tick · enter delete · esc cancel", classes="modal-hint"),
            classes="modal",
        )

    @work(group="command")
    async def run_command(self, text: str) -> None:
        """Slash commands, run in a worker because push_screen_wait needs one."""

        current = self.agent_thread_config["configurable"]["thread_id"]

        if command == "help":
            await self._note(
                "/help    this list\n"
                "/list    every conversation so far\n"
                "/name    title this conversation\n"
                "/load    resume a conversation\n"
                "/delete  remove conversations")

        elif command == "list":
            lines = []
            for i, (thread_id, title, updated_at) in enumerate(list_sessions(self.sqlite_connection), start=1):
                mark = "[b]›[/b]" if thread_id == current else " "
                lines.append(f"{mark} {i}. {title or '(untitled)'}  [dim]{updated_at}[/dim]")
            await self._note("\n".join(lines) or "no sessions yet")

        elif command == "name":
            title = await self.push_screen_wait(NamePrompt())
            if title:
                set_session_title(self.sqlite_connection, current, title)
                await self._note(f"named this conversation “{title}”")

        elif command == "load":
            sessions = list_sessions(self.sqlite_connection)
            if not sessions:
                await self._note("no saved sessions yet", failed=True)
                return
            thread_id = await self.push_screen_wait(SessionPicker(sessions, current))
            if thread_id and thread_id != current:
                self.agent_thread_config["configurable"]["thread_id"] = thread_id
                await self.reload_transcript()

        elif command == "delete":
            sessions = list_sessions(self.sqlite_connection)
            doomed = await self.push_screen_wait(SessionDeleter(sessions, current))
            for thread_id in doomed or []:
                delete_session(self.sqlite_connection, thread_id)
            if doomed:
                await self._note(f"deleted {len(doomed)} session(s)")

        else:
            await self._note(f"{command} unrecognized. Try /help.", failed=True)

        self.transcript.anchor()

    async def _note(self, text: str, failed: bool = False) -> None:
        classes = "turn note failed" if failed else "turn note"
        await self.transcript.mount(Static(text, classes=classes))
        self.transcript.anchor()

# ---- 9. /new and deleting the session you are sitting in ----
async def case_new_and_self_delete():
    """/new gives a clean thread, and /delete may take the current one.

    Both matter because /load leaves you inside someone else's conversation with
    no way back to an empty context.
    """
    import tempfile
    from langgraph.checkpoint.sqlite.aio import AsyncSqliteSaver
    from llmtui.tui import SessionDeleter

    path = tempfile.mktemp(suffix=".sqlite")
    async with AsyncSqliteSaver.from_conn_string(path) as saver:
        await saver.setup()
        connection = sqlite3.connect(path, check_same_thread=False)
        connection.execute("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sessions (thread_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,"
                           " title TEXT, created_at TEXT, updated_at TEXT)")

        agent = create_agent(
            model=ScriptedModel(responses=[ai_text("First answer."), ai_text("Second answer.")]),
            tools=[search_books],
            checkpointer=saver,
        )
        namer = ScriptedModel(responses=[AIMessage(content="First Chat"),
                                         AIMessage(content="Second Chat")])
        first = str(uuid.uuid4())
        app = LlmTui(agent, namer, connection, {"configurable": {"thread_id": first}})

        async with app.run_test() as pilot:
            app.query_one("#prompt").value = "first question"
            await pilot.press("enter")
            await asyncio.sleep(1.6)
            await pilot.pause()
            had_history = len(list(app.query(AssistantTurn))) == 1

            # ---- /new ----
            app.query_one("#prompt").value = "/new"
            await pilot.press("enter")
            await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
            await pilot.pause()
            second = app.agent_thread_config["configurable"]["thread_id"]

            check("9  /new starts a clean thread", [
                ("the first turn had left history", had_history),
                ("thread_id changed", second != first),
                ("transcript cleared of old turns",
                 len(list(app.query(AssistantTurn))) == 0),
                ("context meter reset", app.status.ctx_used == 0),
                ("old session still on disk",
                 connection.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM checkpoints WHERE thread_id = ?",
                                    (first,)).fetchone()[0] > 0),
            ])

            # give the new thread some history of its own
            app.query_one("#prompt").value = "second question"
            await pilot.press("enter")
            await asyncio.sleep(1.6)
            await pilot.pause()

            # ---- /delete, taking the current session with it ----
            app.query_one("#prompt").value = "/delete"
            await pilot.press("enter")
            await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
            await pilot.pause()
            screen = app.screen
            offered = list(screen.query_one("#picker", SelectionList).options) \
                if isinstance(screen, SessionDeleter) else []
            current_is_offered = any(
                o.value == second for o in offered) if offered else False

            # tick every session, current included, then confirm
            screen.query_one("#picker", SelectionList).select_all()
            await pilot.pause()
            await pilot.press("enter")
            await asyncio.sleep(0.6)
            await pilot.pause()

            third = app.agent_thread_config["configurable"]["thread_id"]
            left = connection.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM sessions").fetchone()[0]
            checkpoints_left = connection.execute(
                "SELECT count(*) FROM checkpoints WHERE thread_id IN (?, ?)",
                (first, second)).fetchone()[0]

            check("9b /delete can take the current session", [
                ("the current session was offered for deletion", current_is_offered),
                ("rolled onto a brand new thread", third not in (first, second)),
                ("session rows gone", left == 0),
                ("checkpoints gone for both deleted threads", checkpoints_left == 0),
                ("transcript is empty", len(list(app.query(AssistantTurn))) == 0),
                ("app still usable", app.status.state == "ready"),
            ])
        connection.close()


async def main():
    await case_new_and_self_delete()
    await case_scroll()

Both done. 12/12 TUI, 8/8 middleware.

**`/new`** rolls a fresh `uuid7` thread, clears the transcript, and resets the status bar's context meter, tok/s and elapsed — those described the old thread and would otherwise sit there lying. It also cancels any turn worker still streaming, since that turn belongs to the conversation you're leaving.

**`/delete` is now current-aware.** The filter that excluded the current session is gone; it's offered like any other, marked `· current` in the list so removing it is a choice rather than an accident. If the deletion set includes the thread you're in, it calls the same `start_new_thread()` and tells you so: *"deleted 2 session(s), including this one — started a new conversation"*.

One thing I checked before touching it: `delete_session` runs raw SQL against `checkpoints` and `writes`, and those tables are now owned by `AsyncSqliteSaver` rather than the sync one. Confirmed the async saver creates exactly those two tables, both keyed by `thread_id` — same schema, so no orphaned rows. Worth verifying rather than assuming, since a mismatch would have leaked checkpoint data silently on every delete.

The reasoning behind rolling a new thread rather than just clearing the view: after deleting the current session, `agent_thread_config` still points at a `thread_id` whose checkpoints no longer exist. You'd be in a thread that was just erased, with a status bar quoting a context that's gone. A fresh thread is the only coherent state.

`/help` now lists `/new` and says `/delete` covers "this one included".

The new test drives the whole thing through the real `AsyncSqliteSaver` against a temp file — runs a turn, `/new`s, confirms the old session survives on disk, runs another turn, then `/delete`s everything including the current session and checks both the `sessions` rows and the `checkpoints` rows for both threads are actually gone. That last assertion is the one that would catch a schema mismatch.

"""The agent itself: model, tools, middleware stack, checkpointer."""

from langchain.agents import create_agent
from langchain.agents.middleware import ToolCallLimitMiddleware, ToolErrorMiddleware

from langchain_ollama.chat_models import ChatOllama

from langgraph.graph.state import CompiledStateGraph

from llmtui.config import (
    CONTEXT_SIZE,
    IS_REASONING,
    MAX_TOOL_CALLS,
    MODEL,
    REPETITION_PENALTY,
    SYSTEM_PROMPT_PATH,
    TEMPERATURE,
    TOP_K,
    TOP_P,
)
from llmtui.middleware import on_search_error, repair_tool_calls
from llmtui.tools import TOOLS

with open(SYSTEM_PROMPT_PATH, 'r') as f:
    SYSTEM_PROMPT: str = f.read()


def build_model() -> ChatOllama:
    # values from .env, which are the recommended values from
    # https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B
    # ctx extended according to my 3090 with q8 kv caching
    return ChatOllama(
        model=MODEL,
        reasoning=IS_REASONING,
        num_ctx=CONTEXT_SIZE,
        temperature=TEMPERATURE,
        validate_model_on_init=True,
        top_p=TOP_P,
        top_k=TOP_K,
        repeat_penalty=REPETITION_PENALTY
    )


def build_agent(model: ChatOllama, checkpointer) -> CompiledStateGraph:
    return create_agent(
        model=model,
        tools=TOOLS,
        middleware=[
            ToolCallLimitMiddleware(
                tool_name="search_books",
                run_limit=MAX_TOOL_CALLS
            ),
            ToolErrorMiddleware(
                on_error=on_search_error,
                tools=["search_books"]
            ),
            # after_model custom middleware to fix malformed tool calls
            # https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/middleware/custom#node-style-hooks
            # i am so proud of this one
            repair_tool_calls
        ],
        system_prompt=SYSTEM_PROMPT,
        checkpointer=checkpointer,
    )

content.text:
Draw as the engineer who has to live with the decision, not as a decorator: a diagram earns its place when it lets a cold reader see a mechanism they would otherwise have to assemble from prose — where data flows, which components talk, what changes between two options, what state a request moves through. If a sentence says it faster, write the sentence.

## What to draw

**Depict the mechanism, not its name.** A box labeled "cache" says less than the prose; the path a request takes through it, the two stores it sits between, and the arrow that disappears when the cache is removed say what the words can't. Show the parts that the argument hinges on — the boundary being crossed, the hop being added, the data that moves — and leave out the parts that don't.

**Comparing options?** Draw the difference. Two architectures side by side, a before and an after, the one edge that each option adds or removes — the reader should be able to point at what they are choosing between. A separate labeled box per option, with nothing connecting them to the system, is not a comparison; it is a restated option list.

**Match complexity to the stakes.** A one-hop question is a three-box diagram; a migration that reroutes writes through a queue needs the queue, the writer, the reader, and the ordering arrow. Draw as much as the decision actually turns on — no forced minimalism, no inventory of the whole system either.

**Label the arrows.** An unlabeled arrow is "related somehow"; `writes`, `invalidates`, `polls every 30s` is information. A legend is only worth it when the same encoding (dashed, colored, doubled) repeats; otherwise put the meaning on the mark itself.

## Inline SVG mechanics

These mechanics apply where the page renders inline SVG natively (HTML pages); a markdown-rendered page draws its diagrams in whatever fence that lane's renderer supports, and the skill that owns the lane says which. Hand-author inline `<svg>` with native shapes (`rect`, `circle`, `line`, `polyline`, `path`) and `<text>` — no libraries, no runtime, no external images.

- **Size by `viewBox`.** Set `viewBox="0 0 W H"` and let CSS scale it (`max-width: 100%; height: auto`); choose W and H for the content, not a preset. Wide flows read left-to-right; layered stacks read top-to-bottom.
- **Theme with `currentColor`.** Strokes, text, and arrowheads in `currentColor` inherit the page's foreground in light and dark themes alike; reserve a literal hue for the one element that carries meaning (the option leaned toward, the hop under discussion), and make sure it reads on both grounds.
- **Arrowheads are markers or polygons.** A `<defs><marker>` referenced by `marker-end="url(#arrow)"` (fragment-internal id) or a small `<polygon>` at the line's end — never an image.
- **Keep text legible.** Roughly 11–13px at the drawn scale, `text-anchor` for alignment, short labels (a word or three); explanatory sentences belong in the caption below the figure, not in the drawing.
- **Align to a grid.** Shared baselines and even gaps are most of what makes a hand diagram read as deliberate; eyeballed offsets read as noise.
- **One figure, one claim.** Wrap the `<svg>` in `<figure>` with a `<figcaption>` that states what the picture shows, and give the `<svg>` `role="img"` plus an `aria-label` carrying the same claim for readers who cannot see it.
- **Stay self-contained.** No `<script>`, `<style>`, or `<foreignObject>` inside the SVG; gradients, patterns, and `<use>` reference ids in the same fragment (`href="#id"`). Long decorative path data is a sign the drawing wants a real graphics tool — simplify instead.

Walkthrough · for review

llm-tui Code Walkthrough

How a keystroke becomes an answer on screen, which Textual primitive does what, and where the sync/async boundary runs. Written to be read next to the diff.

tui.py 656 lines tests 12 + 8 cases agent code unchanged cli/ deleted

01 Read it in this order

Bottom-up. Every file here is small except tui.py, and tui.py makes much more sense once you know what it is consuming.

  1. llmtui/config.py (94) — every os.getenv in one place, resolved against a project root. Read _text/_path/_int/_flag; they are the reason a bad .env fails loudly at import.
  2. llmtui/agent.py (64) — the whole agent in one function. Note the middleware order: repair is listed last so it runs first.
  3. app.py (50) — boot. The interesting part is why the saver is an async with around run_async().
  4. llmtui/tui.py — read run_turn first (line 390), then the two pumps below it. Everything else is widgets serving those.
  5. tests/test_tui.py (563) — each case names the bug it exists for. Case 6 is the checkpointer, case 8 is the scroll pin.

02 The shape of it

This is what "bounded to one directory" meant in practice. app.py builds the agent and hands it to the app; tui.py drives it, reads the sessions table, and asks naming.py for a title. No module below the line imports anything from Textual.

03 Boot

app.py is fifty lines and one of them is load-bearing: 

async def main_async() -> None:
    sqlite_connection = connect()          # sync, for the sessions table
    model = build_model()

    async with AsyncSqliteSaver.from_conn_string(SQLITE_DB_PATH) as memory:
        await memory.setup()
        agent = build_agent(model, memory)
        ...
        await LlmTui(...).run_async()

def main() -> None:
    asyncio.run(main_async())

The saver is an async context manager, and the app has to live inside it — hence run_async() rather than run(), with asyncio.run wrapping the whole thing. Get that nesting wrong and the connection closes while the app is still checkpointing.

Two connections, one file. The sessions table goes through a plain sqlite3 connection; checkpoints go through aiosqlite. That is why sessions.connect() sets PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL — two writers on the default journal collide. Both see the same checkpoints and writes tables, which is what lets delete_session clear all three tables in one sync transaction.

04 One turn, end to end

The three things worth checking in review, in order of how easy they are to get wrong:

  • astream_events returns a coroutine. Not an async iterator — awaiting it yields the AsyncGraphRunStream. Forgetting the await fails in a confusing place.
  • The tail work sits outside the finally. _read_usage and the naming call both await, and awaiting inside a finally while the worker is being cancelled just raises CancelledError again. Only turn.finish() — which must run either way — is in the finally.
  • Each tool gets its own task. _pump_tools spawns _watch_tool per call rather than awaiting them in the loop. Await them in sequence and the rows resolve one after another, throwing away concurrency the ToolNode already has.

05 How a tool row settles

The trap this encodes. A row that only checked tc.error would settle a failed search as a green success whenever ToolErrorMiddleware caught the raise first — which is how the app is actually wired. The first version of the test built a bare agent with no middleware and missed exactly that. tc.completed is also a plain bool and is False when the stream object arrives, so it cannot be awaited; completion is output_deltas running dry.

06 Every Textual API in play

APIWhereWhat it does for us
App / run_asyncLlmTui, app.pythe event loop the whole UI lives on
@work(exclusive, group)run_turn 390runs the stream off the handler; a new prompt cancels the last
@on(Input.Submitted)submitted 374declarative handler bound to one widget by selector
VerticalScroll#transcriptthe scrollback
.anchor()6 call sitesfollows new content, releases when the reader scrolls
Markdown.get_streamwrite_answer 186incremental markdown; only the last block re-parses
CollapsibleToolRow, reasoningone-line summary that expands in place
.title (reactive)_row_title 85mutating a row's text without remounting it
set_intervalToolRow.on_mount 90the spinner tick, stopped in resolve()
ModalScreen[T]3 pickerstyped dialogs that return a value
push_screen_waitrun_command 509await a modal's result — needs a worker
Binding(priority=True)SessionDeleter 300claims enter before SelectionList eats it
OptionList / SelectionListpicker / deletersingle and multi select
CSS_PATH + TCSStui.tcssall styling, via theme variables
query / query_onethroughoutCSS-selector widget lookup
run_test() pilottest_tui.pya real app, no terminal — how all 12 cases run

07 The sync/async boundary

This is where the checkpointer bug lived, and it is the thing most worth being suspicious about while reviewing.

CallWhich formWhy
agent.astream_eventsasyncdrives the turn; sync stream_events would block the UI
agent.aget_stateasyncget_state raises NotImplementedError against AsyncSqliteSaver
model.ainvokeasyncsession naming, same reason
sessions.py SQLsyncseparate sqlite3 connection, small and fast; WAL keeps it clear
ToolRow.resolvesyncpure widget mutation, no I/O
scripts/inspect_context.pysyncown process, still uses the sync SqliteSaver on the same file
Why the tests missed it. Every case used MemorySaver, which implements both the sync and async checkpoint APIs. The one component that cannot do async was the one the tests never exercised. Case 6 now runs against a real AsyncSqliteSaver and a temp file for exactly that reason.

08 Where to be skeptical

Places I would push on if I were reviewing this rather than writing it.

  • No human has run it against real Ollama. Every test is headless with a scripted model. Streaming smoothness, spinner cadence and whether the reasoning fold feels abrupt at 24 tok/s are all unverified.
  • _read_usage reads the last AIMessage and breaks. If a turn ends on a tool message or the shape changes, the meter silently stops updating rather than erroring. Deliberate, but it fails quiet.
  • The naming call swallows every exception. A failed title should not lose a turn, but it also means a persistently broken namer is invisible.
  • abort() is never called. action_stop cancels the Textual worker instead, because what abort() does to an in-flight Milvus query is untested. The display stops; the graph finishes its step.
  • One timer per tool row. Fine at three concurrent searches, wasteful if the limit ever rises. A single app-level tick driving all running rows would be cheaper.
  • Five hand-maintained duplicates of framework state remain — the Footer string, the chrome Static, the redundant ctrl+q binding. Catalogued in the API audit, not yet applied.
